#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update.sh — pull latest images and restart the Raven stack on a Vultr box.
#
# Differences from deploy/ec2/update.sh:
#   - Uses the default docker daemon socket (Vultr runs a single daemon;
#     EC2 used a hidden secondary daemon at /run/raven/docker.sock).
#   - Targets deploy/vultr/docker-compose.server.yml.
#
# Usage:
#   ./deploy/vultr/update.sh
#   ./deploy/vultr/update.sh --tag v0.4.1   # pin to a release tag
#   ./deploy/vultr/update.sh --sha abc1234  # pin to a commit SHA
#
set -euo pipefail

COMPOSE="docker compose"
ENV_FILE=".env.server"
COMPOSE_FILE="deploy/vultr/docker-compose.server.yml"

REF=""
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --sha)
      REF="sha-${2::7}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --tag)
      REF="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    *)
      echo "Unknown arg: $1" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done

if [ -n "${REF}" ]; then
  GO_API_IMAGE="ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/go-api:${REF}"
  PYTHON_WORKER_IMAGE="ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/python-worker:${REF}"
  FRONTEND_IMAGE="ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/frontend:${REF}"

  set_or_append() {
    local key="$1" value="$2"
    if grep -q "^${key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
      sed -i "s|^${key}=.*|${key}=${value}|" "$ENV_FILE"
    else
      echo "${key}=${value}" >> "$ENV_FILE"
    fi
  }
  set_or_append GO_API_IMAGE "$GO_API_IMAGE"
  set_or_append PYTHON_WORKER_IMAGE "$PYTHON_WORKER_IMAGE"
  set_or_append FRONTEND_IMAGE "$FRONTEND_IMAGE"
  echo "Pinned to ref: ${REF}"
fi

echo "Pulling images..."
$COMPOSE -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" --env-file "$ENV_FILE" pull

echo "Restarting stack..."
$COMPOSE -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" --env-file "$ENV_FILE" up -d --remove-orphans

echo "Stack status:"
$COMPOSE -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" --env-file "$ENV_FILE" ps

name: Demo deploy

# Triggers
#   - push:  any v* tag from main fires a deploy with that tag's images.
#   - workflow_dispatch: manual re-deploy of an existing tag.
#
# Targets the Vultr demo box at vars.VULTR_DEMO_HOST (e.g. 64.176.97.248).
# SSH key is in secrets.VULTR_SSH_KEY (ed25519). The previous AWS EC2 +
# OIDC + SSM flow has been retired.

on:
  push:
    tags: ['v*']
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: Existing v* tag to deploy
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  wait-for-images:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Wait for service images to be available on GHCR
        env:
          TAG: ${{ github.event.inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # release.yml publishes via docker/metadata-action's {{version}}
          # pattern which strips the leading `v` from the SemVer tag.
          IMG_TAG="${TAG#v}"
          for svc in go-api python-worker frontend; do
            for i in {1..30}; do
              if docker manifest inspect "ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/$svc:$IMG_TAG" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "Found $svc:$IMG_TAG"
                break
              fi
              if [ "$i" = "30" ]; then
                echo "Timed out waiting for $svc:$IMG_TAG"
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "Waiting for $svc:$IMG_TAG (attempt $i/30)..."
              sleep 30
            done
          done

  deploy:
    needs: wait-for-images
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Load SSH key
        uses: webfactory/ssh-agent@a6f90b1f127823b31d4d4a8d96047790581349bd  # v0.9.1
        with:
          ssh-private-key: ${{ secrets.VULTR_SSH_KEY }}

      - name: Trust Vultr host key
        env:
          VULTR_HOST: ${{ vars.VULTR_DEMO_HOST }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p ~/.ssh
          ssh-keyscan -T 10 -H "$VULTR_HOST" >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts

      - name: Deploy via SSH
        env:
          TAG: ${{ github.event.inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
          VULTR_HOST: ${{ vars.VULTR_DEMO_HOST }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IMG_TAG="${TAG#v}"
          # git checkout uses the v-prefixed tag; update.sh `--tag` takes
          # the image-tag form (no v). Stays consistent with what release.yml
          # publishes on GHCR.
          ssh "root@$VULTR_HOST" "set -e && \
            cd /opt/raven && \
            git fetch --tags && \
            git checkout '$TAG' && \
            bash deploy/vultr/update.sh --tag '$IMG_TAG'"

      - name: Smoke-test demo /raven/api/v1/config
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Hits the path-prefixed public-config endpoint through cloudflared.
          # Exercises the tunnel ingress + the Go API's PathPrefix-mounted
          # route group (verifying #626 is live on the deployed box).
          for _ in {1..20}; do
            if curl -fsS https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/api/v1/config | grep -q single_user; then
              echo "OK"; exit 0
            fi
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "Demo API never went green"
          exit 1

  notify:
    needs: deploy
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Send result email via Resend API
        env:
          RESEND_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.RESEND_API_KEY }}
          TAG: ${{ github.event.inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ needs.deploy.result }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          curl -fsS -X POST https://api.resend.com/emails \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESEND_API_KEY" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d "{
              \"from\": \"noreply@ravencloak.org\",
              \"to\": [\"jobinlawrance@gmail.com\"],
              \"subject\": \"[demo] $TAG deploy $OUTCOME\",
              \"text\": \"Tag: $TAG\\nResult: $OUTCOME\\nRun: $RUN_URL\"
            }"

name: Demo deploy

on:
  push:
    tags: ['v*']
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: Existing v* tag to deploy
        required: true

permissions:
  id-token: write     # needed for OIDC
  contents: read

env:
  AWS_REGION: ap-south-1
  ROLE_ARN: arn:aws:iam::${{ vars.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID }}:role/raven-demo-github-deploy
  INSTANCE_TAG_KEY: Name
  INSTANCE_TAG_VALUE: raven-demo-app

jobs:
  wait-for-images:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Wait for service images to be available on GHCR
        env:
          TAG: ${{ github.event.inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # release.yml publishes image tags via docker/metadata-action's
          # {{version}} pattern, which strips the leading `v` from the
          # SemVer tag. The git ref still carries `v` (e.g. v0.4.1) so we
          # normalise to the published image-tag form here.
          IMG_TAG="${TAG#v}"
          for svc in go-api python-worker frontend; do
            for i in {1..30}; do
              if docker manifest inspect "ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/$svc:$IMG_TAG" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "Found $svc:$IMG_TAG"
                break
              fi
              if [ "$i" = "30" ]; then
                echo "Timed out waiting for $svc:$IMG_TAG"
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "Waiting for $svc:$IMG_TAG (attempt $i/30)..."
              sleep 30
            done
          done

  deploy:
    needs: wait-for-images
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Configure AWS credentials via OIDC
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ env.ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Resolve demo instance ID
        id: instance
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INSTANCE_ID=$(aws ec2 describe-instances \
            --filters "Name=tag:${INSTANCE_TAG_KEY},Values=${INSTANCE_TAG_VALUE}" \
                      "Name=instance-state-name,Values=running" \
            --query 'Reservations[0].Instances[0].InstanceId' \
            --output text)
          if [ "$INSTANCE_ID" = "None" ] || [ -z "$INSTANCE_ID" ]; then
            echo "No running demo instance found"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "instance_id=$INSTANCE_ID" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Send update.sh via SSM
        id: ssm
        env:
          TAG: ${{ github.event.inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
          INSTANCE_ID: ${{ steps.instance.outputs.instance_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # git checkout uses the v-prefixed git tag; update.sh `--tag`
          # takes the SemVer string (no v) because that's how release.yml
          # publishes to GHCR. See wait-for-images for the same reasoning.
          IMG_TAG="${TAG#v}"
          # After update.sh pulls the standard frontend image (built with
          # VITE_BASE_PATH=/), swap to the path-prefixed variant for demo
          # so the SPA's asset URLs resolve under /raven/. The variant
          # tag is produced by a follow-up CI matrix (Task #9); until
          # then we use the one-off :raven-prefixed tag.
          FRONTEND_DEMO_IMAGE="ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/frontend:raven-prefixed"
          CMD_ID=$(aws ssm send-command \
            --instance-ids "$INSTANCE_ID" \
            --document-name AWS-RunShellScript \
            --comment "demo deploy $TAG" \
            --parameters "commands=[\"cd /opt/raven && git fetch --tags && git checkout $TAG && bash deploy/ec2/update.sh --tag $IMG_TAG && sed -i 's|^FRONTEND_IMAGE=.*|FRONTEND_IMAGE=$FRONTEND_DEMO_IMAGE|' .env.server && DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/raven/docker.sock docker compose -f deploy/ec2/docker-compose.server.yml --env-file .env.server pull frontend && DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/raven/docker.sock docker compose -f deploy/ec2/docker-compose.server.yml --env-file .env.server up -d --remove-orphans frontend\"]" \
            --timeout-seconds 1800 \
            --query 'Command.CommandId' --output text)
          echo "command_id=$CMD_ID" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Wait for SSM command to complete
        env:
          CMD_ID: ${{ steps.ssm.outputs.command_id }}
          INSTANCE_ID: ${{ steps.instance.outputs.instance_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for i in {1..60}; do
            STATUS=$(aws ssm get-command-invocation \
              --command-id "$CMD_ID" --instance-id "$INSTANCE_ID" \
              --query Status --output text)
            echo "[$i] Status: $STATUS"
            case "$STATUS" in
              Success) exit 0 ;;
              Failed|Cancelled|TimedOut)
                aws ssm get-command-invocation \
                  --command-id "$CMD_ID" --instance-id "$INSTANCE_ID" \
                  --query '{stdout:StandardOutputContent,stderr:StandardErrorContent}'
                exit 1
                ;;
            esac
            sleep 30
          done
          echo "Timed out waiting for SSM command"
          exit 1

      - name: Smoke-test demo /raven/api/v1/config
        run: |
          # Hits the path-prefixed public-config endpoint via cloudflared.
          # demo.raven.ravencloak.org is offline since the DNS cutover;
          # /raven/api/v1/config is publicly reachable, returns JSON, and
          # exercises both the tunnel ingress rule and the Go API's
          # PathPrefix-mounted route group (verifies the fix from #626).
          for _ in {1..20}; do
            if curl -fsS https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/api/v1/config | grep -q single_user; then
              echo "OK"; exit 0
            fi
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "Demo API never went green"
          exit 1

  notify:
    needs: deploy
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Send result email via Resend API
        env:
          RESEND_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.RESEND_API_KEY }}
          TAG: ${{ github.event.inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ needs.deploy.result }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          curl -fsS -X POST https://api.resend.com/emails \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESEND_API_KEY" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d "{
              \"from\": \"noreply@ravencloak.org\",
              \"to\": [\"jobinlawrance@gmail.com\"],
              \"subject\": \"[demo] $TAG deploy $OUTCOME\",
              \"text\": \"Tag: $TAG\\nResult: $OUTCOME\\nRun: $RUN_URL\"
            }"

#   - push:  any v* tag from main fires a deploy with that tag's images.
#   - workflow_dispatch: manual re-deploy of an existing tag.

# Targets the Vultr demo box at vars.VULTR_DEMO_HOST (e.g. 64.176.97.248).
# SSH key is in secrets.VULTR_SSH_KEY (ed25519). The previous AWS EC2 +

              echo "Waiting for $svc:$IMG_TAG (attempt $i/30)..."
              sleep 30
            done
          done

  deploy:
    needs: wait-for-images
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Load SSH key
        uses: webfactory/ssh-agent@a6f90b1f127823b31d4d4a8d96047790581349bd  # v0.9.1
        with:
          ssh-private-key: ${{ secrets.VULTR_SSH_KEY }}

      - name: Trust Vultr host key
        env:
          VULTR_HOST: ${{ vars.VULTR_DEMO_HOST }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p ~/.ssh
          ssh-keyscan -T 10 -H "$VULTR_HOST" >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts

      - name: Deploy via SSH

   ```
   ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 root@64.176.97.248 'chmod 600 /etc/cloudflared/<id>.json && systemctl restart cloudflared'
   ```

5. **Populate `/opt/raven/.env.server`** with real secrets (from the existing AWS box if you have access, or fresh).

Run these in **your** terminal (the `!` prefix runs them in this session if you want the output here, but you can also just run them locally):

```bash
# Generate fresh ed25519 deploy key (passphrase-less for CI)
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/raven-vultr-deploy -N "" -C "github-actions-demo-deploy"

# Add the public half to root@Vultr's authorized_keys
cat ~/.ssh/raven-vultr-deploy.pub | ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 root@64.176.97.248 "umask 077 && mkdir -p ~/.ssh && cat >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys && echo added"

# Push private key + host var to repo (the private key contents are piped via stdin — gh redacts them from chat output)
gh secret   set VULTR_SSH_KEY    < ~/.ssh/raven-vultr-deploy
gh variable set VULTR_DEMO_HOST  --body 64.176.97.248

# Verify (won't show secret values)
gh secret   list | grep -i vultr
gh variable list | grep -i vultr
```

Found a real issue. **Two different tunnel IDs:**

- `config.yml` (just written by bootstrap) → `tunnel: 9bae2af2-f8e8-45ed-aa61-e1eb29182c3c` (from terraform state)

- `credentials-file:` in config points at `/etc/cloudflared/9bae2af2-....json` which **doesn't exist**
- cloudflared.service is running, but it was started 6h ago — **before** the bootstrap overwrote config.yml. So in-memory it's still on the OLD config (using `ac5bd284` tunnel). On restart it'll fail.

1. Get docker stack UP on Vultr first (current iteration step)
2. Test stack works via localhost curl ON the Vultr box (bypassing cloudflared)

content.text:
Here's a single command that fills in the required secrets without overwriting any values you've already set. Generates strong randoms for the 3 mandatory secrets, leaves anything you've already populated alone, and sets the demo-specific defaults.

**Run this on your laptop** (the secrets are generated *on the Vultr box*, never echoed in chat):

```bash
ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 root@64.176.97.248 'bash -s' <<'REMOTE'
set -euo pipefail
cd /opt/raven

# Backup existing .env.server before mutation
[ -f .env.server ] && cp .env.server ".env.server.bak.$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
touch .env.server
chmod 600 .env.server

# set_if_empty KEY [DEFAULT]   — sets KEY if missing OR currently empty.
# If DEFAULT is empty, generates a 32-char random.
set_if_empty() {
  local key="$1"
  local default="${2:-}"
  if grep -qE "^${key}=" .env.server; then
    local current
    current="$(grep -E "^${key}=" .env.server | head -1 | cut -d= -f2-)"
    [ -n "$current" ] && return 0
    if [ -z "$default" ]; then
      default="$(openssl rand -base64 32 | tr -d '/+=' | head -c 32)"
    fi
    # Use a delimiter that won't clash with the value
    sed -i "s|^${key}=$|${key}=${default}|" .env.server
  else
    if [ -z "$default" ]; then
      default="$(openssl rand -base64 32 | tr -d '/+=' | head -c 32)"
    fi
    printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$default" >> .env.server
  fi
}

# Required by deploy/ec2/docker-compose.server.yml (the ${VAR:?required} ones)
set_if_empty POSTGRES_PASSWORD
set_if_empty SUPERTOKENS_API_KEY
set_if_empty ZO_ROOT_USER_PASSWORD

# Reasonable defaults — fine to leave as-is
set_if_empty POSTGRES_USER             raven
set_if_empty POSTGRES_DB               raven
set_if_empty ZO_ROOT_USER_EMAIL        admin@ravencloak.org

# Demo-specific: path-prefix routing + path-baked frontend image
set_if_empty RAVEN_PATH_PREFIX         /raven
set_if_empty FRONTEND_IMAGE            ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/frontend:raven-prefixed

# update.sh will overwrite these per --tag, but set sensible initial values
set_if_empty GO_API_IMAGE              ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/go-api:main
set_if_empty PYTHON_WORKER_IMAGE       ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/python-worker:main

# LLM cost fuse
set_if_empty RAVEN_LLM_DAILY_USD_CAP   5.00

echo "=== .env.server keys (values redacted) ==="
grep -E '^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*=' .env.server | sed 's/=.*$/=…/'
echo
echo "=== size: $(wc -c < .env.server) bytes ==="
echo
echo "=== dry-run compose config (looks for any remaining required vars) ==="
docker compose -f deploy/ec2/docker-compose.server.yml --env-file .env.server config >/dev/null && echo "OK — compose accepts the env file." || echo "FAIL — see error above"
REMOTE
```

**What it does:**
- Backs up existing `.env.server` to `.env.server.bak.<timestamp>`
- For each key: if missing or empty, fills in (random secrets where applicable, defaults otherwise)
- `set_if_empty` *only* writes when the value is empty — anything you've already populated stays
- `chmod 600` for safety
- Dry-runs `docker compose config` at the end to surface any remaining required vars I missed

If it prints `OK — compose accepts the env file.` at the end, we're clear to re-trigger the workflow. If it prints a `required variable X is missing` for something else, paste that here and I'll add it to the script.

ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 root@64.176.97.248 'bash -s' <<'REMOTE'
set -euo pipefail
cd /opt/raven

# Read current values
PG_USER=$(grep -E '^POSTGRES_USER=' .env.server | cut -d= -f2-)
PG_PASS=$(grep -E '^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=' .env.server | cut -d= -f2-)
PG_DB=$(grep -E '^POSTGRES_DB=' .env.server | cut -d= -f2-)

# Helper: set var if missing/empty in .env.server
set_if_empty() {
  local key="$1" default="$2"
  if grep -qE "^${key}=" .env.server; then
    local cur; cur="$(grep -E "^${key}=" .env.server | head -1 | cut -d= -f2-)"
    [ -n "$cur" ] && return 0
    sed -i "s|^${key}=$|${key}=${default}|" .env.server
  else
    printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$default" >> .env.server

}

Tunnel `ac5bd284-...` is healthy + connected (location: bom09/Mumbai), in your CLoudflare account (`4112a97db0506e...`). It's just missing Cloudflare-side DNS + ingress rules for any hostname.

I don't have a Cloudflare API token in my session (terraform manages tunnel `9bae2af2`, not this one), so I can't add the route via terraform/CLI. **Quickest path: add the route via Cloudflare dashboard.**

## Steps in Cloudflare dashboard

1. Open **Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels** in the Cloudflare dashboard for your `ravencloak.org` account.
2. Find the tunnel with ID starting `ac5bd284-...` (the name might be "raven-vultr-demo" or similar, whatever you named it when you created it).
3. Click into it → **Public Hostnames** tab → **Add a public hostname**.
4. Add **two** entries pointing at the Vultr box's loopback services:

   | Subdomain | Domain | Path | Service |
   |-----------|--------|------|---------|
   | `vultr-demo` | `ravencloak.org` | `raven/api/*` | `http://localhost:8081` |
   | `vultr-demo` | `ravencloak.org` | `raven/*`     | `http://localhost:3080` |

   (You can use any subdomain you prefer — replace `vultr-demo` everywhere if you want a different name.)

5. Save.

Cloudflare will auto-create the DNS record (`vultr-demo.ravencloak.org` → CNAME → `ac5bd284-….cfargotunnel.com`).

Once that's done, **I'll smoke-test end-to-end via `https://vultr-demo.ravencloak.org/raven/api/v1/config`**. If it returns `{"single_user":false}`, the entire stack is proven (Cloudflare → tunnel → Vultr cloudflared → docker stack → go-api). Then we cut over the production `demo.ravencloak.org` to this tunnel in a follow-up.

Tell me when the route is saved and what hostname you chose.

content.text:
That's the fix. **CNAME is correct, but no Public Hostname routes were saved on tunnel `ac5bd284`.** Cloudflare doesn't know what to do with the request, hence the edge 404.

## Add the public hostnames on tunnel `ac5bd284`

**Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels → click the `ac5bd284-...` tunnel → Public Hostnames tab → "Add a public hostname"**

Add **TWO entries** in this order (order matters — first match wins):

### Entry 1 (more specific path — must be first)
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Subdomain | `vultr-demo` |
| Domain | `ravencloak.org` |
| Path | `raven/api/.*` |
| Service Type | `HTTP` |
| URL | `localhost:8081` |

Then click **"Additional application settings"** at the bottom — leave defaults.

### Entry 2 (catch-all for non-API paths)
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Subdomain | `vultr-demo` |
| Domain | `ravencloak.org` |
| Path | `raven/.*` |
| Service Type | `HTTP` |
| URL | `localhost:3080` |

Save each. Cloudflare may also offer to auto-create the DNS record on save — say "no/skip" (you already created the CNAME manually).

After both are saved and the tunnel reloads (usually instant), tell me and I'll smoke-test again. The response should change from a Cloudflare-edge 404 (no headers from origin) to **`{"single_user":false}` from Go API** with `x-trace-id` + `content-security-policy` headers — that's the unambiguous proof the full path works.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update.sh — pull latest images and restart the Raven stack on a Vultr box.
#
# Differences from deploy/ec2/update.sh:
#   - Uses the default docker daemon socket (Vultr runs a single daemon;
#     EC2 used a hidden secondary daemon at /run/raven/docker.sock).
#   - Targets deploy/vultr/docker-compose.server.yml.
#
# Usage:
#   ./deploy/vultr/update.sh
#   ./deploy/vultr/update.sh --tag v0.4.1   # pin to a release tag
#   ./deploy/vultr/update.sh --sha abc1234  # pin to a commit SHA
#
set -euo pipefail

COMPOSE="docker compose"
ENV_FILE=".env.server"
# The compose file in deploy/ec2/ is platform-agnostic — the EC2-vs-Vultr
# distinction was the secondary docker socket (an env var, not in the YAML).
# Reusing it here avoids drift between deploys.
COMPOSE_FILE="deploy/ec2/docker-compose.server.yml"

REF=""
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --sha)
      REF="sha-${2::7}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --tag)
      REF="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    *)
      echo "Unknown arg: $1" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done

if [ -n "${REF}" ]; then
  GO_API_IMAGE="ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/go-api:${REF}"
  PYTHON_WORKER_IMAGE="ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/python-worker:${REF}"
  FRONTEND_IMAGE="ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/frontend:${REF}"

  set_or_append() {
    local key="$1" value="$2"
    if grep -q "^${key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
      sed -i "s|^${key}=.*|${key}=${value}|" "$ENV_FILE"
    else
      echo "${key}=${value}" >> "$ENV_FILE"
    fi
  }
  set_or_append GO_API_IMAGE "$GO_API_IMAGE"
  set_or_append PYTHON_WORKER_IMAGE "$PYTHON_WORKER_IMAGE"
  set_or_append FRONTEND_IMAGE "$FRONTEND_IMAGE"
  echo "Pinned to ref: ${REF}"
fi

echo "Pulling images..."
$COMPOSE -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" --env-file "$ENV_FILE" pull

echo "Restarting stack..."
$COMPOSE -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" --env-file "$ENV_FILE" up -d --remove-orphans

echo "Stack status:"
$COMPOSE -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" --env-file "$ENV_FILE" ps

content.subject: Clear stale rebase metadata (preserve working tree)
content.description: `.git/rebase-merge/` points at already-merged feat/billing-plans-comparison-page rebased onto cd657adf (PR #614, merged). Use `git rebase --quit` (NOT --abort) to clear the state without touching the working tree, which holds the demo-path-prefix work.

content.subject: Commit demo-path-prefix work with Signed-off-by
content.description: Stage 9 modified files + 3 expanded-scope files: docker-compose.demo.yml (port mappings + RAVEN_PATH_PREFIX + VITE_BASE_PATH build arg), deploy/ansible/group_vars/demo.yml (hostname cutover + raven_path_prefix), deploy/ansible/roles/raven-stack/templates/env.server.j2 (add RAVEN_PATH_PREFIX). Skip terraform.tfstate.backup (gitignored) and node-compile-cache. Single commit with `git commit -s`, no AI attribution.

content.subject: Run local lint + tests before push
content.description: Per repo rules: golangci-lint v2.11.4 (--new-from-rev=HEAD), ruff for Python if Python touched, frontend lint + Playwright. ALL must pass before push — CI lint failures are unacceptable per stored feedback.

content.subject: Push branch + open PR + queue auto-merge
content.description: `git push -u origin feat/demo-path-prefix`, `gh pr create` with summary + test plan, then `gh pr merge <N> --auto --squash` immediately per CLAUDE.md.

content.subject: After PR merges, deploy to 64.176.97.248 prod
content.description: Deploy has NOT happened on 64.176.97.248. Box is bare — no docker/cloudflared/etc. The /raven/ response we observed is coming from the OLD AWS EC2 demo via the updated tunnel config. Need to either (a) properly provision this Vultr box with full ansible playbook OR (b) revert tunnel config and keep AWS demo until proper migration. Mismatch with my earlier 'completed' assumption.

content.subject: Decommission AWS EC2 raven-demo-app instance (after cutover validated)
content.description: Once new box is serving demo.ravencloak.org/raven/ end-to-end and validated, retire the AWS EC2 instance via terraform destroy on the demo's ec2.tf resources OR keep for one week as warm fallback. Coordinate with the DNS cutover — don't tear down before traffic is confirmed flowing to new box.

content.subject: URGENT: fix PR #625 — mount ALL routes under root group
content.description: PR #625 only moved /healthz under `root := router.Group(cfg.Server.PathPrefix)`. All other registrations still on bare `router`. Result: every /raven/api/v1/* request 404s in prod RIGHT NOW. Fix: replace `router.GET/POST/Group/...` with `root.GET/POST/Group/...` for every route registration (keep middleware `.Use()` on router). For PathPrefix="" the behavior is unchanged. Add a smoke test that hits a public route with PathPrefix set so this never regresses.

content.description: Built locally + pushed to ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/frontend:raven-prefixed (linux/amd64) with VITE_BASE_PATH=/raven/ + VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/api/v1. Sha256 16f6cb9bed... Available on GHCR; AWS box still needs FRONTEND_IMAGE override to use it.

Plus update.sh + demo-deploy.yml to use the -raven suffix for frontend on demo. Auto-merge, tag v0.4.1.

content.subject: Follow-up: fix cosign signing config conflicts in release.yml
content.description: Two release.yml jobs failing on cosign v2 breaking change: 'Go binaries' (goreleaser-managed cosign step) and 'Frontend bundle' (direct cosign sign-blob step). Both error: 'cannot specify service URLs and use signing config'. Newer cosign rejects --oidc-issuer when a signing-config is present. Fix: either remove --oidc-issuer flag (let signing-config provide it) OR pin cosign to older version. Replace deprecated --output-signature/--output-certificate with --bundle. NOT blocking demo-deploy — these are for GitHub Release artifacts only. Separate PR.

git commit -s -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
feat(demo): build frontend-raven variant in CI, fix nginx + Dockerfile build args

Closes the gap left by #625 / the Vultr cutover (#628): the public demo
needs a frontend built with VITE_BASE_PATH=/raven/ and a same-origin API
base URL, with nginx that reverse-proxies /raven/{api,auth,webhooks}/*
to go-api. Three things were broken:

1. **frontend/nginx.conf** — the `location ~ ^(?:/[^/]+)?/assets/` regex
   added in #625 set cache headers but had no try_files/alias/rewrite,
   so nginx tried to serve `/raven/assets/foo` from filesystem
   `/usr/share/nginx/html/raven/assets/foo` — 404. SPA never booted
   behind /raven. Replaced with explicit proxy locations for the app
   paths + a /raven/ prefix-strip rewrite (inside the location, not at
   server level, so the proxy blocks still win). Backwards-compatible:
   for root deployments (VITE_BASE_PATH=/) the /raven/* locations are
   inert.

2. **frontend/Dockerfile** — only VITE_BASE_PATH was promoted from ARG
   to a form Vite can actually read at build time. VITE_API_URL,
   VITE_API_BASE_URL, VITE_API_DOMAIN, VITE_LIVEKIT_URL were declared
   as ARGs but never made it into Vite's env, so build-arg overrides
   silently fell back to frontend/.env.production. Now writes all five
   to .env.production.local (Vite's highest-precedence file in
   production mode) just before `npm run build`.

3. **No CI build of the path-prefixed variant** — was tracked as a
   manual one-off (the `:raven-prefixed` tag I built locally yesterday).
   Adds a `frontend-raven` matrix entry to both .github/workflows/
   docker.yml (main + PR builds) and release.yml (tag-triggered
   multi-arch with cosign signing + SBOM attestations). Variant gets
   VITE_BASE_PATH=/raven/ + URLs under `${RAVEN_DEMO_BASE_URL ||
   https://demo.ravencloak.org}`. SaaS frontend tag stays unchanged.

Plus two small wirings:

4. **deploy/vultr/update.sh + .env.server.example** — default
   FRONTEND_IMAGE to `frontend-raven:<ref>` since the Vultr box is
   always demo (path-prefixed). update.sh already overrides the var on
   every --tag run; this just changes the image name it constructs.

   bug that doubled `/api/v1` in the URL (`${VITE_API_BASE_URL}/api/v1
   /config`). Every other src/api/* file treats VITE_API_BASE_URL as
   already containing `/api/v1`; this one location appended it again,
   producing `/raven/api/v1/api/v1/config` on path-prefixed builds.

Signed-off-by: Jobin Lawrance <jobinlawrance@gmail.com>

Five fixes bundled (one PR because they all need to ship together for the demo image to actually work):

```nginx
# What #625 shipped:
location ~ ^(?:/[^/]+)?/assets/ {   # adds cache headers
    expires 1y; ...
}                                    # …but no try_files/alias/rewrite,
                                     # so nginx tries to serve files
                                     # from filesystem /raven/assets/* → 404
```

The SPA never booted behind `/raven/` because every asset request 404'd. Replaced with explicit `proxy_pass` blocks for `/raven/{api,auth,webhooks}/*` (longer-prefix-wins so they match before the catch-all) + a `/raven/` prefix-strip rewrite **inside** the location (NOT at server level, so the proxy blocks still win). ### 2. `frontend/Dockerfile` — only `VITE_BASE_PATH` was reaching Vite

Added to both `.github/workflows/docker.yml` (main + PR) and `.github/workflows/release.yml` (tag + multi-arch + cosign + SBOM). Variant builds with:

- `VITE_BASE_PATH=/raven/`
- `VITE_API_URL=${RAVEN_DEMO_BASE_URL}/raven`
- `VITE_API_BASE_URL=${RAVEN_DEMO_BASE_URL}/raven/api/v1`
- `VITE_API_DOMAIN=${RAVEN_DEMO_BASE_URL}`

Where `RAVEN_DEMO_BASE_URL` defaults to `https://demo.ravencloak.org` and can be overridden via repo var. Published as `ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/frontend-raven:<version>` (and `:latest` on main). The SaaS `frontend` tag is unchanged.

### 4. `deploy/vultr/update.sh` + `.env.server.example`

Default `FRONTEND_IMAGE` to `frontend-raven:<ref>` since the Vultr box is always the path-prefixed demo. `update.sh --tag` continues to overwrite this per-run.

### 5. `frontend/src/stores/server-config.ts` — existing /api/v1-doubling bug

```diff
- `${VITE_API_BASE_URL}/api/v1/config`
+ `${VITE_API_BASE_URL}/config`
```

Every other `src/api/*` file already treats `VITE_API_BASE_URL` as ending in `/api/v1` (e.g. `const base = import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL ?? '/api/v1'`). # Runbook: cut `demo.ravencloak.org` over from AWS to Vultr

**Status**: pending (operational steps below have not been executed yet)
**Estimated time**: ~15 min hands-on + ~5 min DNS propagation
**Reversibility**: full, ~5 min via DNS flip-back
**Risk**: low — both stacks remain runnable during cutover; the only
shared resource is Cloudflare DNS

## Background

`demo.ravencloak.org` currently routes to a cloudflared connector on an
**AWS EC2** instance (`raven-demo-app`, public IP `65.0.104.188`, in
`ap-south-1`). That stack runs pre-#625 code — broken behind the new
`/raven/*` path-prefixed ingress rules.

A parallel **Vultr** stack (`64.176.97.248`) has been provisioned and
proven via the public-IP URL `http://64.176.97.248:13080/raven/` (see
#628 for provisioning, #631 for the path-prefixed CI image). Its
cloudflared connector is already running, but bound to a **different**
tunnel (`ac5bd284-c908-4c7d-8666-f6e8e824c693`) than the one DNS
currently points at (`9bae2af2-f8e8-45ed-aa61-e1eb29182c3c`).

Cutover means: route `demo.ravencloak.org` through the Vultr tunnel
instead of the AWS one, then decommission AWS in a follow-up.

## Tunnel topology — before / after

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `demo.ravencloak.org` CNAME → | `9bae2af2-….cfargotunnel.com` (terraform-managed) | `ac5bd284-….cfargotunnel.com` (created out-of-band) |
| Connector for that tunnel | cloudflared on AWS EC2 | cloudflared on Vultr |
| Ingress rules on tunnel | terraform: `/raven/api/.*` → `localhost:8081`, `/raven/.*` → `localhost:3080` (AWS box) | dashboard: same two rules, on the Vultr tunnel |
| Old tunnel (`9bae2af2`) | active, terraform-managed | dormant; decommission with AWS |

## Pre-flight checks (do not skip)

Run all of these on your laptop. If any fails, fix before proceeding.

```bash
# 1. Vultr stack is healthy end-to-end via the public IP. Replace
#    asset hash with whatever index-*.js the current build emits.
curl -sf http://64.176.97.248:13080/raven/api/v1/config \
  | grep -q single_user && echo "✓ API responds with JSON"

curl -sf -o /dev/null -w "asset HTTP %{http_code}\n" \
  "http://64.176.97.248:13080$(curl -s http://64.176.97.248:13080/raven/ \
    | grep -oE '/raven/assets/index-[^"]+\.js' | head -1)"

# 2. Vultr cloudflared is connected to the tunnel.
ssh root@64.176.97.248 'systemctl is-active cloudflared && \
  journalctl -u cloudflared -n 10 --no-pager | grep -c "Registered tunnel connection"'
# expect: active, plus a non-zero "Registered tunnel connection" count

# 3. AWS demo is still up (so we have a rollback target).
curl -sI https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/api/v1/config \
  | head -1   # any 200/404 from Go's gin (with `x-trace-id` header) is fine — proves AWS is reachable
```

## Cutover steps

### Step 1 — add Public Hostnames on the Vultr tunnel (Cloudflare dashboard)

Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels → click into tunnel `ac5bd284-c908-4c7d-8666-f6e8e824c693` → **Public Hostnames** tab → **Add a public hostname**.

Add **two** entries in this order (more specific first):

| Subdomain | Domain | Path | Service |
|----|----|----|----|
| `demo` | `ravencloak.org` | `raven/api/.*` | `http://localhost:8081` |
| `demo` | `ravencloak.org` | `raven/.*`     | `http://localhost:3080` |

Click **Additional application settings** → leave defaults.
Save each entry.

When prompted to create/overwrite the DNS record, **decline** — we'll handle DNS explicitly in Step 2 so we can verify+roll back independently.

### Step 2 — verify ingress is published before touching DNS

Cloudflare propagates ingress rules to connectors within ~5s. Confirm:

```bash
ssh root@64.176.97.248 'journalctl -u cloudflared -n 20 --no-pager' \
  | grep -i 'ingress\|configuration update\|reload' | tail -5
```

You should see a recent log line about a config update. If nothing appears within a minute, retry the Cloudflare save.

### Step 3 — flip the DNS CNAME

Cloudflare dashboard → `ravencloak.org` zone → **DNS** → **Records** → click the `demo` row → edit:

| Field | Before | After |
|----|----|----|
| Target | `9bae2af2-….cfargotunnel.com` | `ac5bd284-c908-4c7d-8666-f6e8e824c693.cfargotunnel.com` |
| Proxy status | Proxied (orange) | unchanged |
| TTL | Auto | unchanged |

Save. Cloudflare's edge picks up the new CNAME within ~30s.

### Step 4 — smoke test

```bash
# Within ~30s after the DNS save:
for _ in {1..6}; do
  curl -sS -o /tmp/resp -D /tmp/headers -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" \
    https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/api/v1/config
  if grep -q 'single_user' /tmp/resp; then
    echo "✓ JSON received from new Vultr stack"
    break
  fi
  sleep 5
done

# Confirm response came from the right origin:
# - go-api's middleware adds x-trace-id; AWS path was getting Go's 404 page
# - bundle digest should match the frontend-raven image you just published
grep -i 'x-trace-id' /tmp/headers   # presence proves Vultr go-api responded
curl -s https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/ \
  | grep -oE '/raven/assets/index-[^"]+\.js' | head -1
```

If any of those fail, go to **Rollback** below.

### Step 5 — stop the AWS cloudflared connector

We **don't terraform-destroy AWS yet** — keeping it as a warm rollback target for ~24h after cutover. Just stop the cloudflared service so it stops trying to serve the now-orphaned tunnel:

```bash
# Via AWS SSM (preferred — keeps SSH closed):
aws ssm send-command --region ap-south-1 \
  --instance-ids $(aws ec2 describe-instances --region ap-south-1 \
    --filters 'Name=tag:Name,Values=raven-demo-app' \
              'Name=instance-state-name,Values=running' \
    --query 'Reservations[0].Instances[0].InstanceId' --output text) \
  --document-name AWS-RunShellScript \
  --comment 'stop cloudflared post-cutover' \
  --parameters 'commands=["systemctl stop cloudflared && systemctl disable cloudflared"]'
```

After this, tunnel `9bae2af2` has zero connectors. Cloudflare keeps the
tunnel registered (it's a billing/free-tier resource that stays in your
account) but it serves no traffic.

## Rollback (executable in ~2 min)

If Step 4 fails:

1. Cloudflare DNS → `demo` row → flip Target back to `9bae2af2-….cfargotunnel.com`. Save.
2. The AWS cloudflared is still running (Step 5 hasn't happened yet), so traffic resumes via AWS within ~30s.
3. Investigate the Vultr-side failure (cloudflared logs on Vultr, Public Hostname config on `ac5bd284`).
4. Fix, retry from Step 4.

If Step 5 already ran (AWS cloudflared stopped) and you need to roll back: re-enable + start AWS cloudflared via the same SSM pattern (`systemctl enable --now cloudflared`), then flip DNS back.

## Post-cutover follow-ups (separate PRs)

- **Terraform import** of the now-canonical tunnel `ac5bd284` and replace `cloudflare_tunnel.demo` + `cloudflare_tunnel_config.demo` references. Drop the orphaned `9bae2af2` resource. Touches `deploy/terraform/demo/cloudflare.tf` + `terraform import` blocks.
- **AWS decommission**: `terraform destroy` of `aws_instance.demo` + IAM + S3 backup bucket + SSM parameters. Tracked as Task #11.
- **Vultr lockdown**: now that the demo serves through cloudflared, the public-IP ports `13080` + `18081` are no longer needed. Either add a Vultr cloud-firewall rule restricting them to SSH-only, OR rebind compose ports back to `127.0.0.1:` in `docker-compose.override.yml` on the box.
- **Frontend image cleanup**: retire the one-off `ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/frontend:raven-prefixed` tag I hand-built — every release tag now produces `frontend-raven:<version>` via CI (#631).

## What success looks like

- `curl https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/api/v1/config` → `{"single_user":false}` with `x-trace-id` header
- `curl https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/` → SPA HTML referencing `/raven/assets/index-….js`
- Browser load of `https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/` → boots the Vue app, can hit the login page (SuperTokens calls via same-origin nginx proxy)
- Vultr `journalctl -u cloudflared` shows connection events; AWS box shows the same when re-enabled

tunnel (`ac5bd284-c908-4c7d-8666-f6e8e824c693`) than the one DNS
currently points at (`9bae2af2-f8e8-45ed-aa61-e1eb29182c3c`).

Cutover means: route `demo.ravencloak.org` through the Vultr tunnel
instead of the AWS one, then decommission AWS in a follow-up.

## Tunnel topology — before / after

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `demo.ravencloak.org` CNAME → | `9bae2af2-….cfargotunnel.com` (terraform-managed) | `ac5bd284-….cfargotunnel.com` (created out-of-band) |
| Connector for that tunnel | cloudflared on AWS EC2 | cloudflared on Vultr |
| Ingress rules on tunnel | terraform: `/raven/api/.*` → `localhost:8081`, `/raven/.*` → `localhost:3080` (AWS box) | dashboard: same two rules, on the Vultr tunnel |
| Old tunnel (`9bae2af2`) | active, terraform-managed | dormant; decommission with AWS |

## Pre-flight checks (do not skip)

Run all of these on your laptop. If any fails, fix before proceeding.

```bash
# 1. Vultr stack is healthy end-to-end via the public IP. Replace
#    asset hash with whatever index-*.js the current build emits.
curl -sf http://64.176.97.248:13080/raven/api/v1/config \
  | grep -q single_user && echo "✓ API responds with JSON"

curl -sf -o /dev/null -w "asset HTTP %{http_code}\n" \
  "http://64.176.97.248:13080$(curl -s http://64.176.97.248:13080/raven/ \
    | grep -oE '/raven/assets/index-[^"]+\.js' | head -1)"

# 2. Vultr cloudflared is connected to the tunnel.
ssh root@64.176.97.248 'systemctl is-active cloudflared && \
  journalctl -u cloudflared -n 10 --no-pager | grep -c "Registered tunnel connection"'
# expect: active, plus a non-zero "Registered tunnel connection" count

# 3. AWS demo is still up (so we have a rollback target).
curl -sI https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/api/v1/config \
  | head -1   # any 200/404 from Go's gin (with `x-trace-id` header) is fine — proves AWS is reachable
```

## Cutover steps

### Step 1 — add Public Hostnames on the Vultr tunnel (Cloudflare dashboard)

Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels → click into tunnel `ac5bd284-c908-4c7d-8666-f6e8e824c693` → **Public Hostnames** tab → **Add a public hostname**.

Add **two** entries in this order (more specific first):

| Subdomain | Domain | Path | Service |
|----|----|----|----|
| `demo` | `ravencloak.org` | `raven/api/.*` | `http://localhost:8081` |
| `demo` | `ravencloak.org` | `raven/.*`     | `http://localhost:3080` |

Click **Additional application settings** → leave defaults.
Save each entry.

When prompted to create/overwrite the DNS record, **decline** — we'll handle DNS explicitly in Step 2 so we can verify+roll back independently.

### Step 2 — verify ingress is published before touching DNS

Cloudflare propagates ingress rules to connectors within ~5s. Confirm:

```bash
ssh root@64.176.97.248 'journalctl -u cloudflared -n 20 --no-pager' \
  | grep -i 'ingress\|configuration update\|reload' | tail -5
```

You should see a recent log line about a config update. If nothing appears within a minute, retry the Cloudflare save.

### Step 3 — flip the DNS CNAME

Cloudflare dashboard → `ravencloak.org` zone → **DNS** → **Records** → click the `demo` row → edit:

| Field | Before | After |
|----|----|----|
| Target | `9bae2af2-….cfargotunnel.com` | `ac5bd284-c908-4c7d-8666-f6e8e824c693.cfargotunnel.com` |
| Proxy status | Proxied (orange) | unchanged |
| TTL | Auto | unchanged |

Save. Cloudflare's edge picks up the new CNAME within ~30s.

### Step 4 — smoke test

```bash
# Within ~30s after the DNS save:
for _ in {1..6}; do
  curl -sS -o /tmp/resp -D /tmp/headers -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" \
    https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/api/v1/config
  if grep -q 'single_user' /tmp/resp; then
    echo "✓ JSON received from new Vultr stack"
    break
  fi
  sleep 5
done

# Confirm response came from the right origin:
# - go-api's middleware adds x-trace-id; AWS path was getting Go's 404 page
# - bundle digest should match the frontend-raven image you just published
grep -i 'x-trace-id' /tmp/headers   # presence proves Vultr go-api responded
curl -s https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/ \
  | grep -oE '/raven/assets/index-[^"]+\.js' | head -1
```

If any of those fail, go to **Rollback** below.

### Step 5 — stop the AWS cloudflared connector

We **don't terraform-destroy AWS yet** — keeping it as a warm rollback target for ~24h after cutover. Just stop the cloudflared service so it stops trying to serve the now-orphaned tunnel:

```bash
# Via AWS SSM (preferred — keeps SSH closed):
aws ssm send-command --region ap-south-1 \
  --instance-ids $(aws ec2 describe-instances --region ap-south-1 \
    --filters 'Name=tag:Name,Values=raven-demo-app' \
              'Name=instance-state-name,Values=running' \
    --query 'Reservations[0].Instances[0].InstanceId' --output text) \
  --document-name AWS-RunShellScript \
  --comment 'stop cloudflared post-cutover' \
  --parameters 'commands=["systemctl stop cloudflared && systemctl disable cloudflared"]'
```

After this, tunnel `9bae2af2` has zero connectors. Cloudflare keeps the
tunnel registered (it's a billing/free-tier resource that stays in your
account) but it serves no traffic.

## Rollback (executable in ~2 min)

If Step 4 fails:

1. Cloudflare DNS → `demo` row → flip Target back to `9bae2af2-….cfargotunnel.com`. Save.
2. The AWS cloudflared is still running (Step 5 hasn't happened yet), so traffic resumes via AWS within ~30s.
3. Investigate the Vultr-side failure (cloudflared logs on Vultr, Public Hostname config on `ac5bd284`).
4. Fix, retry from Step 4.

If Step 5 already ran (AWS cloudflared stopped) and you need to roll back: re-enable + start AWS cloudflared via the same SSM pattern (`systemctl enable --now cloudflared`), then flip DNS back.

## Post-cutover follow-ups (separate PRs)

- **Terraform import** of the now-canonical tunnel `ac5bd284` and replace `cloudflare_tunnel.demo` + `cloudflare_tunnel_config.demo` references. Drop the orphaned `9bae2af2` resource. Touches `deploy/terraform/demo/cloudflare.tf` + `terraform import` blocks.
- **AWS decommission**: `terraform destroy` of `aws_instance.demo` + IAM + S3 backup bucket + SSM parameters. Tracked as Task #11.
- **Vultr lockdown**: now that the demo serves through cloudflared, the public-IP ports `13080` + `18081` are no longer needed. Either add a Vultr cloud-firewall rule restricting them to SSH-only, OR rebind compose ports back to `127.0.0.1:` in `docker-compose.override.yml` on the box.
- **Frontend image cleanup**: retire the one-off `ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/frontend:raven-prefixed` tag I hand-built — every release tag now produces `frontend-raven:<version>` via CI (#631).

## What success looks like

- `curl https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/api/v1/config` → `{"single_user":false}` with `x-trace-id` header
- `curl https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/` → SPA HTML referencing `/raven/assets/index-….js`
- Browser load of `https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/` → boots the Vue app, can hit the login page (SuperTokens calls via same-origin nginx proxy)
- Vultr `journalctl -u cloudflared` shows connection events; AWS box shows the same when re-enabled

# Dispatching Parallel Agents

## Overview

You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.

When you have multiple unrelated failures (different test files, different subsystems, different bugs), investigating them sequentially wastes time. Each investigation is independent and can happen in parallel.

**Core principle:** Dispatch one agent per independent problem domain. Let them work concurrently.

## When to Use

```dot
digraph when_to_use {
    "Multiple failures?" [shape=diamond];
    "Are they independent?" [shape=diamond];
    "Single agent investigates all" [shape=box];
    "One agent per problem domain" [shape=box];
    "Can they work in parallel?" [shape=diamond];
    "Sequential agents" [shape=box];
    "Parallel dispatch" [shape=box];

    "Multiple failures?" -> "Are they independent?" [label="yes"];
    "Are they independent?" -> "Single agent investigates all" [label="no - related"];
    "Are they independent?" -> "Can they work in parallel?" [label="yes"];
    "Can they work in parallel?" -> "Parallel dispatch" [label="yes"];
    "Can they work in parallel?" -> "Sequential agents" [label="no - shared state"];
}
```

**Use when:**
- 3+ test files failing with different root causes
- Multiple subsystems broken independently
- Each problem can be understood without context from others
- No shared state between investigations

**Don't use when:**
- Failures are related (fix one might fix others)
- Need to understand full system state
- Agents would interfere with each other

## The Pattern

### 1. Identify Independent Domains

Group failures by what's broken:
- File A tests: Tool approval flow
- File B tests: Batch completion behavior
- File C tests: Abort functionality

Each domain is independent - fixing tool approval doesn't affect abort tests.

### 2. Create Focused Agent Tasks

Each agent gets:
- **Specific scope:** One test file or subsystem
- **Clear goal:** Make these tests pass
- **Constraints:** Don't change other code
- **Expected output:** Summary of what you found and fixed

### 3. Dispatch in Parallel

```typescript
// In Claude Code / AI environment
Task("Fix agent-tool-abort.test.ts failures")
Task("Fix batch-completion-behavior.test.ts failures")
Task("Fix tool-approval-race-conditions.test.ts failures")
// All three run concurrently
```

### 4. Review and Integrate

When agents return:
- Read each summary
- Verify fixes don't conflict
- Run full test suite
- Integrate all changes

## Agent Prompt Structure

Good agent prompts are:
1. **Focused** - One clear problem domain
2. **Self-contained** - All context needed to understand the problem
3. **Specific about output** - What should the agent return?

```markdown
Fix the 3 failing tests in src/agents/agent-tool-abort.test.ts:

1. "should abort tool with partial output capture" - expects 'interrupted at' in message
2. "should handle mixed completed and aborted tools" - fast tool aborted instead of completed
3. "should properly track pendingToolCount" - expects 3 results but gets 0

These are timing/race condition issues. Your task:

1. Read the test file and understand what each test verifies
2. Identify root cause - timing issues or actual bugs?
3. Fix by:
   - Replacing arbitrary timeouts with event-based waiting

```

## Common Mistakes

**❌ Too broad:** "Fix all the tests" - agent gets lost
**✅ Specific:** "Fix agent-tool-abort.test.ts" - focused scope

**❌ No context:** "Fix the race condition" - agent doesn't know where
**✅ Context:** Paste the error messages and test names

**❌ No constraints:** Agent might refactor everything
**✅ Constraints:** "Do NOT change production code" or "Fix tests only"

**❌ Vague output:** "Fix it" - you don't know what changed
**✅ Specific:** "Return summary of root cause and changes"

## When NOT to Use

**Related failures:** Fixing one might fix others - investigate together first
**Need full context:** Understanding requires seeing entire system
**Exploratory debugging:** You don't know what's broken yet
**Shared state:** Agents would interfere (editing same files, using same resources)

- batch-completion-behavior.test.ts: 2 failures (tools not executing)
- tool-approval-race-conditions.test.ts: 1 failure (execution count = 0)

```
Agent 2 → Fix batch-completion-behavior.test.ts
Agent 3 → Fix tool-approval-race-conditions.test.ts
```

- Agent 2: Fixed event structure bug (threadId in wrong place)
- Agent 3: Added wait for async tool execution to complete

**Integration:** All fixes independent, no conflicts, full suite green

1. **Parallelization** - Multiple investigations happen simultaneously
2. **Focus** - Each agent has narrow scope, less context to track
3. **Independence** - Agents don't interfere with each other
4. **Speed** - 3 problems solved in time of 1

## Verification

After agents return:
1. **Review each summary** - Understand what changed
2. **Check for conflicts** - Did agents edit same code?
3. **Run full suite** - Verify all fixes work together
4. **Spot check** - Agents can make systematic errors

- 6 failures across 3 files
- 3 agents dispatched in parallel
- All investigations completed concurrently
- All fixes integrated successfully
- Zero conflicts between agent changes

# Context (you don't have prior conversation history)

There's a Vultr box (64.176.97.248) running the Raven demo via docker compose. During emergency demo-unbreaking, two ports were temporarily bound to `0.0.0.0` so the demo could be reached via the public IP without going through Cloudflare:
- `0.0.0.0:13080:8080` for the frontend
- `0.0.0.0:18081:8081` for the go-api

That state lives in `/opt/raven/docker-compose.override.yml` on the Vultr box (not in the repo). It was a debugging convenience.

After the Cloudflare cutover (runbook at `docs/runbooks/demo-cutover.md`), traffic flows through cloudflared again, so the public ports are no longer needed. The lockdown means: rebind to `127.0.0.1:` only, so external traffic must enter via cloudflared (which connects outbound from the box, no inbound port exposure).

# Your task

Draft a PR that codifies the locked-down state for future bootstraps + provides a one-shot script to lock down the existing live box.

Specifically:

1. **Branch**: off latest `main`. Name it `chore/vultr-lockdown-public-ports`.
2. **Files to touch** (all under `deploy/vultr/`):
   - `bootstrap.sh` — make sure freshly-bootstrapped boxes don't write a public-port override. The current bootstrap doesn't write that file, but add a note (in a comment block) explaining that the override is for debugging only and should be removed/replaced before production. If `bootstrap.sh` doesn't currently mention overrides, ADD a section that explicitly creates a clean `/opt/raven/docker-compose.override.yml` with the correct go-api `entrypoint` override + healthcheck override (for the path-prefix healthz) BUT NO public-port bindings. Match the existing-bootstrap style (idempotent, root-only, prints progress).
   - **New file** `deploy/vultr/lockdown.sh` — operator-side one-shot script. SSHes to the Vultr box, rewrites `/opt/raven/docker-compose.override.yml` to remove the `0.0.0.0:13080` / `0.0.0.0:18081` lines, restarts go-api + frontend, verifies they're now only listening on 127.0.0.1, prints external probe instructions for the operator to verify.
   - `.env.server.example` — no change needed unless you find something stale.
3. **Files NOT to touch**: anything outside `deploy/vultr/`. Don't touch `cloudflare.tf` or AWS terraform — those are parallel PRs.
4. **Use the same docker-compose.override.yml content I'll describe** — the go-api needs `entrypoint: ["/app/api"]` (skips dotenvx) and a healthcheck override that hits `/raven/healthz`:

   ```yaml
   services:
     go-api:
       entrypoint: ["/app/api"]
       healthcheck:
         test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:8081/raven/healthz"]
   ```

   That's the locked-down baseline. NO `ports:` overrides → docker uses base compose's `127.0.0.1:` bindings.

5. **Sign off the commit** with `-s` (DCO; commit must end with `Signed-off-by: Jobin Lawrance <jobinlawrance@gmail.com>`). Conventional commit message. No `Co-Authored-By:` trailers.
6. **Open PR with `gh pr create`** against `main`. **Queue auto-merge with `gh pr merge <N> --auto --squash`** — this one is safe to auto-merge once CI passes (the script doesn't execute itself; operator runs it manually after cutover).
7. **In the PR body**:
   - State that this depends on the cutover (runbook PR #632) being executed before `lockdown.sh` should be run.
   - Include the one-line invocation: `bash deploy/vultr/lockdown.sh root@64.176.97.248`
   - Mention how to roll back if needed (`git checkout <prev-sha> docker-compose.override.yml` on the box + restart)

Repo conventions:
- Squash-merge only; DCO sign-off required
- `shellcheck deploy/vultr/*.sh` must be clean
- Make all `.sh` files executable (`chmod +x`)

Verify before opening PR:
- `shellcheck deploy/vultr/bootstrap.sh deploy/vultr/lockdown.sh` clean
- `bash -n` (syntax-only) clean on both scripts
- Diff only touches `deploy/vultr/`

Report back (under 250 words): branch name, PR number, files changed, shellcheck status, the exact command to run on cutover day.

- SSH: `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 root@64.176.97.248`
- Existing tunnel that you MUST leave alone:
  - systemd unit: `cloudflared.service` (NOT `cloudflared-epoqgrid.service` — that string was a copy-paste from a different project's runbook; this box only has `cloudflared.service`)
  - Its config: `/etc/cloudflared/config.yml`
  - Its tunnel UUID: `ac5bd284-c908-4c7d-8666-f6e8e824c693` (credentials JSON of the same name)
  - It serves `demo.ravencloak.org` via the Raven docker stack at `/opt/raven`
- cloudflared binary is already installed at `/usr/local/bin/cloudflared`
- The Raven docker stack is running. OpenObserve listens on `127.0.0.1:5080` inside the box — that's the target for the new tunnel.

# Goal (this phase only)

Get to the point where the new tunnel is ready to be created — that means logging into Cloudflare via cloudflared, which is interactive (prints a browser URL and waits). Do NOT create the tunnel or modify DNS yet — that's the next phase, after I tell you the user has authorized.

# Phase 1 — do this NOW, then stop

1. SSH in. Confirm:
   - `systemctl is-active cloudflared.service` returns `active`
   - `systemctl is-active cloudflared-observability.service` returns `inactive` or `unknown` (we don't want to step on an existing one with the new name)
   - `ls /etc/cloudflared/` — note what's there

2. Check whether `/root/.cloudflared/cert.pem` already exists (it would, if the box has been logged in before for a different zone):
   - If present: print its mtime and `cloudflared tunnel list 2>&1 | head -20` to see existing tunnels under this cert. If `ravencloak.org` is already an authorized zone on this cert, skip step 3 and report "auth already in place, ready for Phase 2".
   - If absent or cert doesn't cover ravencloak.org: proceed to step 3.

3. Kick off `cloudflared tunnel login` in the background with output captured:
   ```bash
   nohup cloudflared tunnel login > /tmp/cf-login-$$.log 2>&1 &
   echo $! > /tmp/cf-login.pid
   ```

   - Anything unusual you noticed (existing tunnels, existing cert, etc.)

- Touch `cloudflared.service`, `/etc/cloudflared/config.yml`, or `ac5bd284-….json`
- Create the new tunnel yet (`cloudflared tunnel create`)
- Touch any DNS records
- Write any new systemd unit
- Modify anything under `/opt/raven`

You'll be asked to:
1. Verify `/root/.cloudflared/cert.pem` was updated (mtime newer than your Phase 1 timestamp)

4. Move credentials: `mv /root/.cloudflared/<uuid>.json /etc/cloudflared/<uuid>.json && chmod 600 /etc/cloudflared/<uuid>.json`
5. Write `/etc/cloudflared/observability.yml` (NOT `config.yml` — that's the existing tunnel's file):
   ```yaml
   tunnel: <uuid>
   credentials-file: /etc/cloudflared/<uuid>.json
   ingress:
     - hostname: observability.ravencloak.org
       service: http://localhost:5080
     - service: http_status:404
   ```
6. Write `/etc/systemd/system/cloudflared-observability.service` — copy the shape of `/etc/systemd/system/cloudflared.service` but swap `--config /etc/cloudflared/observability.yml` and update Description. Do NOT reuse the unit name.
7. `systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl enable --now cloudflared-observability.service`
8. Verify:
   - `systemctl is-active cloudflared-observability.service` returns `active`
   - `journalctl -u cloudflared-observability -n 30 --no-pager | grep -c "Registered tunnel connection"` returns non-zero
   - `systemctl is-active cloudflared.service` STILL returns `active` (didn't accidentally break it)
   - `curl -sI https://observability.ravencloak.org/` returns 2xx or 3xx from OpenObserve (not a 530/521/404 from Cloudflare)

For now though, **only do Phase 1 and stop**. Report back with the auth URL + your observations.

Return under 300 words:
- Auth URL (one-line, copyable)
- Whether cert.pem already existed + its mtime
- Confirmation that `cloudflared.service` is still healthy
- Any pre-existing tunnels visible under the current auth
- Anything else surprising

input.message:
Phase 3 — repeat the same pattern for the demo. Goal: cut `demo.ravencloak.org` over from AWS (tunnel `raven-demo` / `9bae2af2-…`) to a fresh Vultr-side tunnel.

# Pre-flight (verify, then proceed)

The Raven docker stack on this box is healthy (10 containers, 21h uptime). Key services on loopback:
- frontend nginx at `127.0.0.1:3080` — image `ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/frontend:raven-self-contained`, which reverse-proxies `/raven/{api,auth,webhooks}/*` internally to go-api. So **a single ingress rule** is sufficient.
- go-api at `127.0.0.1:8081` (don't need to route to this directly — frontend nginx handles it)

Existing tunnels under the cert (from your Phase 1 report): `raven`, `raven-demo`, `ravencloak`, `raven auth`. **Don't pick `raven-demo`** — that's the AWS-side tunnel we're replacing. Use `raven-demo-vultr` to avoid confusion.

# Steps

1. `cloudflared tunnel create raven-demo-vultr` — capture the UUID.

2. Write `/etc/cloudflared/demo.yml`:
   ```yaml
   tunnel: <uuid>
   credentials-file: /etc/cloudflared/<uuid>.json
   ingress:
     - hostname: demo.ravencloak.org
       service: http://localhost:3080
     - service: http_status:404
   ```
   (Single ingress, since the frontend container's nginx already handles /raven/* → static SPA AND /raven/api/* → go-api.)

3. Move credentials: `mv /root/.cloudflared/<uuid>.json /etc/cloudflared/<uuid>.json && chmod 600 /etc/cloudflared/<uuid>.json`.

4. Write `/etc/systemd/system/cloudflared-demo.service` — copy the shape of the working `cloudflared-observability.service` you wrote in Phase 2, but swap config path + Description. New unit name: `cloudflared-demo.service`.

5. `systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl enable --now cloudflared-demo.service`.

6. **Before touching DNS**, confirm the new connector is registered:
   - `systemctl is-active cloudflared-demo.service` → `active`
   - `journalctl -u cloudflared-demo -n 30 --no-pager | grep -c "Registered tunnel connection"` → 4

7. **Now flip DNS**: `cloudflared tunnel route dns --overwrite-dns raven-demo-vultr demo.ravencloak.org`. The pre-existing record currently points at `9bae2af2-…cfargotunnel.com` (AWS tunnel); this rewrites to the new one.

8. Wait ~20s for Cloudflare's edge to pick up the new CNAME, then verify EXACTLY this (4 lines):
   - `systemctl is-active cloudflared-demo.service` → `active`
   - `systemctl is-active cloudflared-observability.service` → `active` (untouched)
   - `systemctl is-active cloudflared-epoqgrid.service` → `active` (untouched)
   - `curl -sS -o /tmp/r https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/api/v1/config -w "HTTP %{http_code} ct=%{content_type}\n" && cat /tmp/r && echo` — expect HTTP 200, `application/json`, body `{"single_user":false}` (this proves Cloudflare → new tunnel → Vultr cloudflared-demo → frontend nginx → go-api → JSON, end-to-end)

9. Bonus check: `curl -sI https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/` → 200 with `x-trace-id` header somewhere downstream (go-api middleware) and HTML body. Confirms SPA shell loads too.

10. Print tunnel UUID + CNAME + that it's serving correctly.

# Rollback (if step 8 fails)

`cloudflared tunnel route dns --overwrite-dns raven-demo demo.ravencloak.org` — flips DNS back to the AWS tunnel. Then investigate, fix, retry. AWS connector stays running this whole time, so rollback is ~30s of Cloudflare cache.

# Don't do

- Don't touch `cloudflared-epoqgrid.service` or `cloudflared-observability.service`
- Don't touch the AWS box (it stays running with `cloudflared` on tunnel `raven-demo` — orphaned but harmless after DNS flip; user will shut it down later)
- Don't run `lockdown.sh` — separate step after this validates
- Don't commit anything to the repo

Report under 300 words: tunnel UUID, smoke-test results (all four verification lines), any drift you noticed, any unexpected output.

content.text:
🎯 **Found the actual bug:**

```
demo.ravencloak.org.epoqgrid.com is already configured to route to your tunnel tunnelID=c508cea5-…
```

The cloudflared CLI **appended `.epoqgrid.com`** to the hostname — created a bogus `demo.ravencloak.org.epoqgrid.com` DNS record instead of touching the real `demo.ravencloak.org`. The actual `demo.ravencloak.org` CNAME was never changed; it still points at the AWS tunnel (`raven-demo` / `9bae2af2-…` with connectors at `65.0.104.188`).

This happens because `cert.pem` has multiple zones authorized (both `ravencloak.org` and `epoqgrid.com` from the multi-tenant setup) and cloudflared CLI picked epoqgrid as the default zone.

## Fix — dashboard is fastest

I can't change DNS without a Cloudflare API token, so this needs you in the dashboard:

**Cloudflare → `ravencloak.org` zone → DNS → Records → `demo` row → edit:**

| Field | Current value | New value |
|-------|--------------|-----------|
| Target | `9bae2af2-f8e8-45ed-aa61-e1eb29182c3c.cfargotunnel.com` (AWS) | `c508cea5-e96e-4786-85f6-d4700a07f98a.cfargotunnel.com` (Vultr) |
| Proxy | Proxied (orange) | leave proxied |
| TTL | Auto | leave |

Save. ~30s for Cloudflare's edge to pick up the new CNAME, then `demo.ravencloak.org` will route to Vultr.

**Also recommended (cleanup):** Delete the bogus `demo.ravencloak.org.epoqgrid.com` record under the `epoqgrid.com` zone — it serves no purpose.

Tell me when the DNS edit is done and I'll smoke-test from outside. Same drill as before — expect HTTP 200 + `application/json` + `{"single_user":false}` once routing flips.

Current state on the box:

| Config | State |
|--------|-------|
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` in `.env.server` | **EMPTY** (keys exist, values blank) |
| `RAVEN_SUPERTOKENS_API_KEY` + connection | set ✓ |

| Provider list (Google etc.) | "managed via SuperTokens Core multitenancy API" — **not yet registered** |
| SuperTokens `apiBasePath` | hardcoded to `/auth` |

There's a **routing mismatch** I should flag before we set anything in Google Console:

The go-api mounts everything under `/raven` (path-prefix), so the `/auth/*` route is actually at `/raven/auth/*` externally. But `apiBasePath` in `supertokens_init.go` is hardcoded `/auth`. SuperTokens uses that to (a) match incoming requests and (b) construct the callback URL it tells Google to use. With current code, SuperTokens would expect Google to redirect to `https://demo.ravencloak.org/auth/callback/google` — which doesn't exist (the real route is at `/raven/auth/callback/google`).

So we need a small code change before Google OAuth can work end-to-end. Pieces to wire up:

1. **Code**: make `apiBasePath` honor `RAVEN_PATH_PREFIX` (one-line fix → `/raven/auth`)
2. **Google Cloud Console**: create an OAuth 2.0 Client ID, set authorized origins + redirect URIs
3. **`.env.server` on Vultr**: populate `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` + `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`
4. **SuperTokens Core**: register the Google ThirdParty provider via its multitenancy API (one curl call to the supertokens container)
5. **Rebuild + redeploy go-api** with the apiBasePath fix
6. **Verify** the SPA's "Sign in with Google" button works

content.text:
Two tracks in parallel — I'll start the code change now while you do Google Console.

## Google Cloud Console — your steps

1. **Console**: https://console.cloud.google.com/

2. **Project**: pick or create one (e.g. `raven-demo`). Top bar → project selector → New Project.

3. **OAuth consent screen** (left nav → APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen):
   - User Type: **External** (so anyone with a Google account can sign in to the demo)
   - App name: `Raven Demo`
   - User support email: your email
   - App domain → Authorized domains: add **`ravencloak.org`**
   - Developer contact: your email
   - Scopes: defaults are fine (`userinfo.email`, `userinfo.profile`, `openid`)
   - Test users: skip (External app in "Testing" mode lets you sign in without verification while Test Users are listed — or "publish" the app to skip that limit, but unverified)
   - Save.

4. **Create OAuth Client ID** (left nav → APIs & Services → Credentials → Create Credentials → OAuth client ID):
   - Application type: **Web application**
   - Name: `Raven Demo Frontend`
   - **Authorized JavaScript origins** — add:
     ```
     https://demo.ravencloak.org
     ```
   - **Authorized redirect URIs** — add EXACTLY:
     ```
     https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/auth/callback/google
     ```
     (This must match what SuperTokens will send — path-prefixed.)
   - Click Create.

5. A modal appears with **Client ID** and **Client Secret**.

49			},

53				WebsiteDomain:   cfg.WebsiteDomain,
54				APIBasePath:     &apiBasePath,

feat(auth): honor RAVEN_PATH_PREFIX in SuperTokens APIBasePath

Until now `apiBasePath` and `websiteBasePath` were hardcoded to `/auth`
in `internal/auth/supertokens_init.go`. With the path-prefix work from
#625/#626, the Go API mounts every route under cfg.Server.PathPrefix —
so on the demo the actual `/auth/*` routes live at `/raven/auth/*`. But
the SuperTokens SDK was still configured for `/auth`, which meant:

- Incoming requests at `/raven/auth/...` didn't match the SDK's
  internal path comparison, so the SuperTokens middleware would let
  them through without handling them.
- Generated callback URLs sent to OAuth providers (Google, GitHub, etc.)
  pointed at `https://<APIDomain>/auth/callback/<id>` — a route that
  doesn't exist on the demo. The provider would redirect there and
  hit a 404 (or worse, the SPA fallback).

Fix: extend `SuperTokensInitConfig` with a `PathPrefix` field that's
prepended to both base paths. cmd/api/main.go threads
`cfg.Server.PathPrefix` (already env-bound to `RAVEN_PATH_PREFIX`)
into the call. SaaS (PathPrefix="") behaviour is unchanged — the
empty-string prefix yields the original `/auth`.

Demo callback URL becomes `https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/auth/
callback/google` — which the frontend container's nginx already
reverse-proxies to go-api via the `/raven/auth/` location (added in
#631).

Signed-off-by: Jobin Lawrance <jobinlawrance@gmail.com>
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

content.text:
Docker workflow queued (~15-20 min for multi-arch builds). **While that's running**, you can drop the Client Secret directly onto the box using this command. The secret goes via your local terminal's `read -s` (silent — nothing echoed in chat, nothing in shell history because of the leading space, no temp file).

**Run this on your laptop** (note the **leading space** — that keeps it out of bash history with `HISTCONTROL=ignorespace`; if your shell doesn't have that, paste it from anywhere and `history -d $(history 1)` afterward):

```bash
 read -rs -p 'paste Google Client Secret + Enter: ' GS && echo && \
ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 root@64.176.97.248 \
  "cd /opt/raven && \
   cp .env.server .env.server.bak.\$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ) && \
   sed -i 's|^GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=.*|REDACTED.apps.googleusercontent.com|' .env.server && \
   sed -i 's|^GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=.*|GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=$GS|' .env.server && \
   echo '=== verify (values redacted) ===' && \
   grep ^GOOGLE_ .env.server | sed 's/=.*\$/=…/' && \
   echo '=== length sanity check (secret should be ~24 chars for Google) ===' && \
   awk -F= '/^GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=/ {print \"secret length:\", length(\$2)}' .env.server" && \
unset GS
```

When you run it:
1. It silently waits for you to paste the secret + hit Enter.
2. SSHes in, backs up `.env.server`, sed-replaces both `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` in place.
3. Prints redacted key list and a length check (Google secrets are typically 24 chars — `GOCSPX-...`).
4. Unsets the local env var.

content.text:
Sorry — zsh's `read` doesn't take `-p`. Here's a shell-agnostic version (`printf` for the prompt, then plain `read -rs`):

```bash
 printf 'paste Google Client Secret + Enter: ' && read -rs GS && echo && \
ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 root@64.176.97.248 \
  "cd /opt/raven && \
   cp .env.server .env.server.bak.\$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ) && \
   sed -i 's|^GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=.*|REDACTED.apps.googleusercontent.com|' .env.server && \
   sed -i 's|^GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=.*|GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=$GS|' .env.server && \
   echo '=== verify (values redacted) ===' && \
   grep ^GOOGLE_ .env.server | sed 's/=.*\$/=…/' && \
   echo '=== length sanity check ===' && \
   awk -F= '/^GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=/ {print \"secret length:\", length(\$2)}' .env.server" && \
unset GS
```

Note: leading space + you're already in zsh, so it doesn't go to history if `setopt HIST_IGNORE_SPACE` is set (default in oh-my-zsh).

ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 root@64.176.97.248 'bash -s' <<'REMOTE'
set -e
cd /opt/raven

# 1. Read creds from .env.server (no echo, stays in shell vars only)
SK="$(awk -F= '/^RAVEN_SUPERTOKENS_API_KEY=/ {print $2}' .env.server)"
CID="$(awk -F= '/^GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=/ {print $2}' .env.server)"
GS="$(awk -F= '/^GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=/ {print $2}' .env.server)"

# Sanity: lengths only, no values
echo "supertokens api-key length: ${#SK}"
echo "google client id length:    ${#CID}"
echo "google client secret length: ${#GS}"

# 2. Build the JSON payload to a temp file (no value in command line)
TMP="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$TMP"' EXIT
cat > "$TMP" <<JSON
{
  "config": {
    "thirdPartyId": "google",
    "name": "Google",
    "clients": [
      {
        "clientID": "${CID}",
        "clientSecret": "${GS}"
      }
    ]
  }
}
JSON

# 3. Identify the docker network the raven stack runs on
NET="$(docker inspect ec2-supertokens-1 -f '{{range $k,$v := .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{$k}}{{end}}')"
echo "raven docker network: $NET"

# 4. PUT the Google provider config via a curl container ON the same network.
#    Mount the temp JSON ro so the secret never appears in the curl command.
echo "=== registering google provider in supertokens core ==="
docker run --rm \
  --network "$NET" \
  -v "$TMP":/data.json:ro \
  -e SK="$SK" \
  curlimages/curl:8.10.1 \
  -sS -X PUT \
  -H "api-key: $SK" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @/data.json \
  http://supertokens:3567/recipe/multitenancy/config/thirdparty
echo

# 5. Pull the new go-api image + force-recreate the container so it picks up
#    both the supertokens path-prefix code change AND the new env vars
echo "=== pulling new go-api image ==="
docker compose -f deploy/ec2/docker-compose.server.yml \
  -f docker-compose.override.yml \
  --env-file .env.server pull go-api 2>&1 | tail -5

echo "=== recreating go-api ==="
docker compose -f deploy/ec2/docker-compose.server.yml \
  -f docker-compose.override.yml \
  --env-file .env.server up -d --force-recreate go-api 2>&1 | tail -3

sleep 8
echo "=== container state ==="
docker compose -f deploy/ec2/docker-compose.server.yml \
  -f docker-compose.override.yml \
  --env-file .env.server ps go-api

echo
echo "=== logs (looking for 'Raven API server starting' + apiBasePath confirmation) ==="
docker compose -f deploy/ec2/docker-compose.server.yml \
  -f docker-compose.override.yml \
  --env-file .env.server logs --tail=10 go-api 2>&1 | tail -10
REMOTE

content.text:
# 🎉 Google OAuth is wired end-to-end

SuperTokens responded with a complete, valid Google authorization URL:

```
https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?
  access_type=offline
  &REDACTED.apps.googleusercontent.com
  &include_granted_scopes=true
  &redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fdemo.ravencloak.org%2Fraven%2Fauth%2Fcallback%2Fgoogle
  &response_type=code
  &scope=openid+email
```

The critical bits all line up:
- ✅ Client ID matches what you provided
- ✅ `redirect_uri` is `https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/auth/callback/google` — exactly what you set in Google Console
- ✅ Same response via Cloudflare-tunnel round trip (so the SPA in a real browser will get the same URL)
- ✅ Scopes: `openid+email` (SuperTokens default for Google)

## Browser test

Open **https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/** in a browser:
1. Should load the SPA
2. Click "Sign in with Google" (or whatever the button is on the login page)
3. Should redirect to Google's account picker
4. After consenting, Google redirects back to `/raven/auth/callback/google` → SuperTokens exchanges the code → session cookie is set → SPA picks up the session

If anything fails in the browser flow, share the URL + any console errors and I'll investigate. Most likely failure modes:
- `redirect_uri_mismatch` from Google → means the Console URI doesn't exactly match (trailing slash, http vs https, etc.)
- CORS error on the callback → SuperTokens cookie config might need adjusting for `demo.ravencloak.org` (currently set to `.ravencloak.org` for cross-subdomain — should work)
- SPA's `loginWithGoogle()` button doesn't fire → frontend may need a small tweak

|---|---|

| Google ThirdParty provider in SuperTokens Core | ✅ registered, 1 client |
| `/raven/auth/*` routes reachable | ✅ both localhost + via Cloudflare |
| Authorize URL generation | ✅ correct redirect_uri + client_id |
| End-to-end browser test | ⏳ your turn |

Try it and let me know.
