content.subject: Fix docker.yml paths filter to include source dirs (frontend/src, ai-worker python, etc.)
content.description: Current filter only triggers on Dockerfile / nginx.conf / docker-compose changes. Any TS/Vue change to frontend/src or Go change cmd/... or Python change to ai-worker/raven_worker/** silently skips the image build, leaving the floating :main / :raven-self-contained tags stale relative to source. Needs paths broadened (or split workflow: lint/test on every push, image build gated separately).

content.subject: Backend: pin SuperTokens to header transfer in session.Init (GetTokenTransferMethod)
content.description: SPA is in header mode but backend defaults to cookie response on OAuth callback. Pin via session.Init's GetTokenTransferMethod returning HeaderTransferMethod so the OAuth signinup response surfaces tokens in headers (not cookies), which the SDK then writes to localStorage. Required for the SPA's Session.doesSessionExist() to return true after page reload / mid-session navigation.

content.subject: URGENT: fix PR #625 — mount ALL routes under root group
content.description: PR #625 only moved /healthz under `root := router.Group(cfg.Server.PathPrefix)`. All other registrations still on bare `router`. Result: every /raven/api/v1/* request 404s in prod RIGHT NOW. Fix: replace `router.GET/POST/Group/...` with `root.GET/POST/Group/...` for every route registration (keep middleware `.Use()` on router). For PathPrefix="" the behavior is unchanged. Add a smoke test that hits a public route with PathPrefix set so this never regresses.

content.subject: Follow-up: fix cosign signing config conflicts in release.yml
content.description: Two release.yml jobs failing on cosign v2 breaking change: 'Go binaries' (goreleaser-managed cosign step) and 'Frontend bundle' (direct cosign sign-blob step). Both error: 'cannot specify service URLs and use signing config'. Newer cosign rejects --oidc-issuer when a signing-config is present. Fix: either remove --oidc-issuer flag (let signing-config provide it) OR pin cosign to older version. Replace deprecated --output-signature/--output-certificate with --bundle. NOT blocking demo-deploy — these are for GitHub Release artifacts only. Separate PR.

content.subject: Follow-up: populate users.email from Google session claims
content.description: Real user row in users table has empty email after Google OAuth. supertokens.go's extractSessionClaims reads from AccessTokenPayload but the payload doesn't include email by default. Need OverrideAPIs.SignInUpPost or a backend post-signinup hook that writes email/name from the ThirdParty user info into the SuperTokens session payload (so downstream userLookup gets real values). Separate PR — diagnostic + fix.

content.subject: Diagnose mid-session logout on navigation
content.description: Verified via Playwright: header-mode is correctly wired (st-auth-mode: header sent in request headers, frontend bundle has tokenTransferMethod:`header` baked in, redirect URI matches Google Console). What I CANNOT test from Playwright: actual Google sign-in (no real account / 2FA). Needs user to (a) clear all browser data, (b) sign in fresh, (c) confirm header-mode tokens land in localStorage (st-access-token, st-refresh-token), (d) try the navigation again. If still fails post-clear-and-fresh-sign-in, the issue isn't cookie-related and is likely a backend session-validation or anti-csrf mismatch.

content.subject: Trigger docker.yml on main HEAD to rebuild frontend with header-mode bundle
content.description: PR #670 (header-based session transfer) is merged into main (ebf76654) but never built an image — docker.yml path filter excludes frontend/src/**. Manual dispatch needed to publish a fresh :raven-self-contained.

content.subject: Fix docker.yml paths filter to include source dirs (frontend/src, ai-worker python, etc.)
content.description: Current filter only triggers on Dockerfile / nginx.conf / docker-compose changes. Any TS/Vue change to frontend/src or Go change cmd/... or Python change to ai-worker/raven_worker/** silently skips the image build, leaving the floating :main / :raven-self-contained tags stale relative to source. Needs paths broadened (or split workflow: lint/test on every push, image build gated separately).

content.subject: Backend: pin SuperTokens to header transfer in session.Init (GetTokenTransferMethod)
content.description: SPA is in header mode but backend defaults to cookie response on OAuth callback. Pin via session.Init's GetTokenTransferMethod returning HeaderTransferMethod so the OAuth signinup response surfaces tokens in headers (not cookies), which the SDK then writes to localStorage. Required for the SPA's Session.doesSessionExist() to return true after page reload / mid-session navigation.

content.subject: Follow-up: fix cosign signing config conflicts in release.yml
content.description: Two release.yml jobs failing on cosign v2 breaking change: 'Go binaries' (goreleaser-managed cosign step) and 'Frontend bundle' (direct cosign sign-blob step). Both error: 'cannot specify service URLs and use signing config'. Newer cosign rejects --oidc-issuer when a signing-config is present. Fix: either remove --oidc-issuer flag (let signing-config provide it) OR pin cosign to older version. Replace deprecated --output-signature/--output-certificate with --bundle. NOT blocking demo-deploy — these are for GitHub Release artifacts only. Separate PR.

content.subject: Follow-up: populate users.email from Google session claims
content.description: Real user row in users table has empty email after Google OAuth. supertokens.go's extractSessionClaims reads from AccessTokenPayload but the payload doesn't include email by default. Need OverrideAPIs.SignInUpPost or a backend post-signinup hook that writes email/name from the ThirdParty user info into the SuperTokens session payload (so downstream userLookup gets real values). Separate PR — diagnostic + fix.

content.subject: Diagnose mid-session logout on navigation
content.description: Verified via Playwright: header-mode is correctly wired (st-auth-mode: header sent in request headers, frontend bundle has tokenTransferMethod:`header` baked in, redirect URI matches Google Console). What I CANNOT test from Playwright: actual Google sign-in (no real account / 2FA). Needs user to (a) clear all browser data, (b) sign in fresh, (c) confirm header-mode tokens land in localStorage (st-access-token, st-refresh-token), (d) try the navigation again. If still fails post-clear-and-fresh-sign-in, the issue isn't cookie-related and is likely a backend session-validation or anti-csrf mismatch.

content.subject: Trigger docker.yml on main HEAD to rebuild frontend with header-mode bundle
content.description: PR #670 (header-based session transfer) is merged into main (ebf76654) but never built an image — docker.yml path filter excludes frontend/src/**. Manual dispatch needed to publish a fresh :raven-self-contained.

content.subject: Fix docker.yml paths filter to include source dirs (frontend/src, ai-worker python, etc.)
content.description: Current filter only triggers on Dockerfile / nginx.conf / docker-compose changes. Any TS/Vue change to frontend/src or Go change cmd/... or Python change to ai-worker/raven_worker/** silently skips the image build, leaving the floating :main / :raven-self-contained tags stale relative to source. Needs paths broadened (or split workflow: lint/test on every push, image build gated separately).

content.subject: Backend: pin SuperTokens to header transfer in session.Init (GetTokenTransferMethod)
content.description: SPA is in header mode but backend defaults to cookie response on OAuth callback. Pin via session.Init's GetTokenTransferMethod returning HeaderTransferMethod so the OAuth signinup response surfaces tokens in headers (not cookies), which the SDK then writes to localStorage. Required for the SPA's Session.doesSessionExist() to return true after page reload / mid-session navigation.

content.subject: Follow-up: fix cosign signing config conflicts in release.yml
content.description: Two release.yml jobs failing on cosign v2 breaking change: 'Go binaries' (goreleaser-managed cosign step) and 'Frontend bundle' (direct cosign sign-blob step). Both error: 'cannot specify service URLs and use signing config'. Newer cosign rejects --oidc-issuer when a signing-config is present. Fix: either remove --oidc-issuer flag (let signing-config provide it) OR pin cosign to older version. Replace deprecated --output-signature/--output-certificate with --bundle. content.subject: Follow-up: populate users.email from Google session claims
content.description: Real user row in users table has empty email after Google OAuth. supertokens.go's extractSessionClaims reads from AccessTokenPayload but the payload doesn't include email by default. Need OverrideAPIs.SignInUpPost or a backend post-signinup hook that writes email/name from the ThirdParty user info into the SuperTokens session payload (so downstream userLookup gets real values). Separate PR — diagnostic + fix.

content.subject: Diagnose mid-session logout on navigation
content.description: Verified via Playwright: header-mode is correctly wired (st-auth-mode: header sent in request headers, frontend bundle has tokenTransferMethod:`header` baked in, redirect URI matches Google Console). What I CANNOT test from Playwright: actual Google sign-in (no real account / 2FA). Needs user to (a) clear all browser data, (b) sign in fresh, (c) confirm header-mode tokens land in localStorage (st-access-token, st-refresh-token), (d) try the navigation again. If still fails post-clear-and-fresh-sign-in, the issue isn't cookie-related and is likely a backend session-validation or anti-csrf mismatch.

content.subject: Fix docker.yml paths filter to include source dirs (frontend/src, ai-worker python, etc.)
content.description: Current filter only triggers on Dockerfile / nginx.conf / docker-compose changes. Any TS/Vue change to frontend/src or Go change cmd/... or Python change to ai-worker/raven_worker/** silently skips the image build, leaving the floating :main / :raven-self-contained tags stale relative to source. Needs paths broadened (or split workflow: lint/test on every push, image build gated separately).

content.subject: Backend: pin SuperTokens to header transfer in session.Init (GetTokenTransferMethod)
content.description: SPA is in header mode but backend defaults to cookie response on OAuth callback. Pin via session.Init's GetTokenTransferMethod returning HeaderTransferMethod so the OAuth signinup response surfaces tokens in headers (not cookies), which the SDK then writes to localStorage. Required for the SPA's Session.doesSessionExist() to return true after page reload / mid-session navigation.

content.text: **Critical finding**: The /auth/signinup response has tokens in **HEADERS** (`st-access-token`, `st-refresh-token`, `front-token`) — backend IS in header mode! But the browser also has these as cookies. Let me compare values to see who's setting them:

**Mystery solved.** SuperTokens header mode controls the WIRE format only. The SDK's default cookieHandler still writes tokens to `document.cookie` for client-side storage. So cookies on disk ≠ cookie-mode on the wire.

- access token payload valid (exp=2026-05-24T09:54, not expired)
- cookies all present

**The bug isn't SuperTokens — it's our SPA's router guard.** It's running before `auth.init()` resolves, so `sessionExists.value` is still its initial `false` → guard sends you to /login. After login renders, the SDK *then* finishes its async check and confirms session exists, but the redirect has already happened.

5-minute SPA fix: make the router guard `await auth.init()` (or block navigation until the auth store has resolved at least once). No backend change, no auth-platform migration.

**That said**, if you still want to ditch SuperTokens (3rd auth platform burn after Keycloak + Zitadel — fair frustration), realistic options for Go-native + edge:

| Option | Footprint | Effort | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hand-rolled (goth + JWT)** | ~500 LoC, 0 extra processes | ~1 day | `markbates/goth` for OAuth (covers 50+ providers), `golang-jwt` + signed cookies for sessions, your own `users` + `sessions` tables (already exist). Smallest, fastest, fully owned. |
| **Ory Kratos** | Separate Go binary + own Postgres schema | ~3 days | Mature, edge-friendly, well-documented. Adds 1 process + own DB tables. Self-service flows are nice. |
| **Better Auth** | Node sidecar (~30MB) | ~2 days | TypeScript-first, modern, batteries-included. But violates "single Go binary" preference — adds a Node process. |
| **Pocketbase** | Single binary | ~3 days | Replaces Postgres too. Total rewrite of data layer. |

My recommendation: **fix the router guard first** (cheap, confirms the underlying auth works). If you still want to replace, **go hand-rolled with goth** — smallest blast radius, no infra surface added, and your `users` table already exists.

Which do you want? Router-guard fix, hand-rolled replacement, or one of the others?

content.subject: URGENT: fix PR #625 — mount ALL routes under root group
content.description: PR #625 only moved /healthz under `root := router.Group(cfg.Server.PathPrefix)`. All other registrations still on bare `router`. Result: every /raven/api/v1/* request 404s in prod RIGHT NOW. Fix: replace `router.GET/POST/Group/...` with `root.GET/POST/Group/...` for every route registration (keep middleware `.Use()` on router). For PathPrefix="" the behavior is unchanged. Add a smoke test that hits a public route with PathPrefix set so this never regresses.

Plus update.sh + demo-deploy.yml to use the -raven suffix for frontend on demo. Auto-merge, tag v0.4.1.

content.subject: Follow-up: fix cosign signing config conflicts in release.yml
content.description: Two release.yml jobs failing on cosign v2 breaking change: 'Go binaries' (goreleaser-managed cosign step) and 'Frontend bundle' (direct cosign sign-blob step). Both error: 'cannot specify service URLs and use signing config'. Newer cosign rejects --oidc-issuer when a signing-config is present. Fix: either remove --oidc-issuer flag (let signing-config provide it) OR pin cosign to older version. Replace deprecated --output-signature/--output-certificate with --bundle. NOT blocking demo-deploy — these are for GitHub Release artifacts only. Separate PR.

content.subject: Follow-up: populate users.email from Google session claims
content.description: Real user row in users table has empty email after Google OAuth. supertokens.go's extractSessionClaims reads from AccessTokenPayload but the payload doesn't include email by default. Need OverrideAPIs.SignInUpPost or a backend post-signinup hook that writes email/name from the ThirdParty user info into the SuperTokens session payload (so downstream userLookup gets real values). Separate PR — diagnostic + fix.

content.subject: Diagnose mid-session logout on navigation
content.description: Verified via Playwright: header-mode is correctly wired (st-auth-mode: header sent in request headers, frontend bundle has tokenTransferMethod:`header` baked in, redirect URI matches Google Console). What I CANNOT test from Playwright: actual Google sign-in (no real account / 2FA). Needs user to (a) clear all browser data, (b) sign in fresh, (c) confirm header-mode tokens land in localStorage (st-access-token, st-refresh-token), (d) try the navigation again. If still fails post-clear-and-fresh-sign-in, the issue isn't cookie-related and is likely a backend session-validation or anti-csrf mismatch.

content.subject: Trigger docker.yml on main HEAD to rebuild frontend with header-mode bundle
content.description: PR #670 (header-based session transfer) is merged into main (ebf76654) but never built an image — docker.yml path filter excludes frontend/src/**. Manual dispatch needed to publish a fresh :raven-self-contained.

content.subject: Fix docker.yml paths filter to include source dirs (frontend/src, ai-worker python, etc.)
content.description: Current filter only triggers on Dockerfile / nginx.conf / docker-compose changes. Any TS/Vue change to frontend/src or Go change cmd/... or Python change to ai-worker/raven_worker/** silently skips the image build, leaving the floating :main / :raven-self-contained tags stale relative to source. Needs paths broadened (or split workflow: lint/test on every push, image build gated separately).

content.subject: Backend: pin SuperTokens to header transfer in session.Init (GetTokenTransferMethod)
content.description: SPA is in header mode but backend defaults to cookie response on OAuth callback. Pin via session.Init's GetTokenTransferMethod returning HeaderTransferMethod so the OAuth signinup response surfaces tokens in headers (not cookies), which the SDK then writes to localStorage. Required for the SPA's Session.doesSessionExist() to return true after page reload / mid-session navigation.
content.activeForm: Pinning backend SuperTokens to header transfer

Pin via session.Init's GetTokenTransferMethod returning HeaderTransferMethod so the OAuth signinup response surfaces tokens in headers (not cookies), which the SDK then writes to localStorage. Required for the SPA's Session.doesSessionExist() to return true after page reload / mid-session navigation.

I have a clear picture now. The cookies are present and valid (Path=`/`, SameSite=`lax`, on HTTPS), but **`Session.doesSessionExist()` returns false on cold boot** despite the cookies being there. SDK lazy-init race.

Fix: add a cookie-based fallback in `auth.init()` — if SDK says no session but `sFrontToken` cookie is present and not expired, treat as authenticated.

input.subject: Frontend: fix auth.init() cold-boot race — use sFrontToken cookie as fallback
input.description: On cold page load with valid SuperTokens cookies, Session.doesSessionExist() returns false initially (SDK hydration race) → auth store treats as logged out → router guard redirects to /login. Fix: in auth.ts init(), fall back to parsing sFrontToken cookie payload if SDK says no session — if its `up.exp` (session exp ms) is in the future, mark sessionExists=true and read orgId via subsequent /api/v1/me call. SDK catches up shortly after.

content.description: PR #625 only moved /healthz under `root := router.Group(cfg.Server.PathPrefix)`. All other registrations still on bare `router`. Result: every /raven/api/v1/* request 404s in prod RIGHT NOW. Fix: replace `router.GET/POST/Group/...` with `root.GET/POST/Group/...` for every route registration (keep middleware `.Use()` on router). For PathPrefix="" the behavior is unchanged. Add a smoke test that hits a public route with PathPrefix set so this never regresses.

content.subject: URGENT: rebuild + publish frontend image with VITE_BASE_PATH=/raven/
content.description: Built locally + pushed to ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/frontend:raven-prefixed (linux/amd64) with VITE_BASE_PATH=/raven/ + VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/api/v1. Sha256 16f6cb9bed... Available on GHCR; AWS box still needs FRONTEND_IMAGE override to use it.

content.subject: Track 1: cut release tag from main HEAD to redeploy AWS demo
content.description: v0.4.0 tag failed due to workflow bugs (#627). Cut v0.4.1 from main HEAD (3b32f7b5) which includes #625 + #626 + #627. Release + Demo deploy workflows now in_progress.
content.activeForm: Cutting release tag for AWS redeploy

content.subject: After demo-deploy succeeds: override FRONTEND_IMAGE on AWS box
content.description: FRONTEND_IMAGE override is now baked into demo-deploy.yml (via PR #627) so the SSM command runs the sed + pull + restart automatically. Manual override no longer needed.

content.subject: PR: fix release.yml printf + demo-deploy tag/smoke + frontend variant
content.description: Single PR fixing: (1) release.yml manifest printf for multi-arch, (2) demo-deploy.yml strip v-prefix from tag, (3) demo-deploy.yml smoke URL to demo.ravencloak.org/raven/api/v1/config, (4) release.yml frontend matrix entry building VITE_BASE_PATH=/raven/ variant tagged frontend:VERSION-raven. Plus update.sh + demo-deploy.yml to use the -raven suffix for frontend on demo. Auto-merge, tag v0.4.1.

content.subject: Follow-up: fix cosign signing config conflicts in release.yml
content.description: Two release.yml jobs failing on cosign v2 breaking change: 'Go binaries' (goreleaser-managed cosign step) and 'Frontend bundle' (direct cosign sign-blob step). Both error: 'cannot specify service URLs and use signing config'. Newer cosign rejects --oidc-issuer when a signing-config is present. Fix: either remove --oidc-issuer flag (let signing-config provide it) OR pin cosign to older version. Replace deprecated --output-signature/--output-certificate with --bundle. NOT blocking demo-deploy — these are for GitHub Release artifacts only. Separate PR.

content.subject: Follow-up: populate users.email from Google session claims
content.description: Real user row in users table has empty email after Google OAuth. supertokens.go's extractSessionClaims reads from AccessTokenPayload but the payload doesn't include email by default. Need OverrideAPIs.SignInUpPost or a backend post-signinup hook that writes email/name from the ThirdParty user info into the SuperTokens session payload (so downstream userLookup gets real values). Separate PR — diagnostic + fix.

content.subject: Diagnose mid-session logout on navigation
content.description: Verified via Playwright: header-mode is correctly wired (st-auth-mode: header sent in request headers, frontend bundle has tokenTransferMethod:`header` baked in, redirect URI matches Google Console). What I CANNOT test from Playwright: actual Google sign-in (no real account / 2FA). Needs user to (a) clear all browser data, (b) sign in fresh, (c) confirm header-mode tokens land in localStorage (st-access-token, st-refresh-token), (d) try the navigation again. If still fails post-clear-and-fresh-sign-in, the issue isn't cookie-related and is likely a backend session-validation or anti-csrf mismatch.

content.subject: Trigger docker.yml on main HEAD to rebuild frontend with header-mode bundle
content.description: PR #670 (header-based session transfer) is merged into main (ebf76654) but never built an image — docker.yml path filter excludes frontend/src/**. Manual dispatch needed to publish a fresh :raven-self-contained.

content.subject: Fix docker.yml paths filter to include source dirs (frontend/src, ai-worker python, etc.)
content.description: Current filter only triggers on Dockerfile / nginx.conf / docker-compose changes. Any TS/Vue change to frontend/src or Go change cmd/... or Python change to ai-worker/raven_worker/** silently skips the image build, leaving the floating :main / :raven-self-contained tags stale relative to source. Needs paths broadened (or split workflow: lint/test on every push, image build gated separately).

content.subject: Backend: pin SuperTokens to header transfer in session.Init (GetTokenTransferMethod)
content.description: SPA is in header mode but backend defaults to cookie response on OAuth callback. Pin via session.Init's GetTokenTransferMethod returning HeaderTransferMethod so the OAuth signinup response surfaces tokens in headers (not cookies), which the SDK then writes to localStorage. Required for the SPA's Session.doesSessionExist() to return true after page reload / mid-session navigation.
content.activeForm: Pinning backend SuperTokens to header transfer

content.subject: Frontend: fix auth.init() cold-boot race — use sFrontToken cookie as fallback
content.description: On cold page load with valid SuperTokens cookies, Session.doesSessionExist() returns false initially (SDK hydration race) → auth store treats as logged out → router guard redirects to /login. Fix: in auth.ts init(), fall back to parsing sFrontToken cookie payload if SDK says no session — if its `up.exp` (session exp ms) is in the future, mark sessionExists=true and read orgId via subsequent /api/v1/me call. SDK catches up shortly after.

content.subject: Diagnose mid-session logout on navigation
content.description: Verified via Playwright: header-mode is correctly wired (st-auth-mode: header sent in request headers, frontend bundle has tokenTransferMethod:`header` baked in, redirect URI matches Google Console). What I CANNOT test from Playwright: actual Google sign-in (no real account / 2FA). Needs user to (a) clear all browser data, (b) sign in fresh, (c) confirm header-mode tokens land in localStorage (st-access-token, st-refresh-token), (d) try the navigation again. If still fails post-clear-and-fresh-sign-in, the issue isn't cookie-related and is likely a backend session-validation or anti-csrf mismatch.

content.subject: Backend: pin SuperTokens to header transfer in session.Init (GetTokenTransferMethod)
content.description: SPA is in header mode but backend defaults to cookie response on OAuth callback. Pin via session.Init's GetTokenTransferMethod returning HeaderTransferMethod so the OAuth signinup response surfaces tokens in headers (not cookies), which the SDK then writes to localStorage. Required for the SPA's Session.doesSessionExist() to return true after page reload / mid-session navigation.

content.subject: Frontend: fix auth.init() cold-boot race — use sFrontToken cookie as fallback
content.description: On cold page load with valid SuperTokens cookies, Session.doesSessionExist() returns false initially (SDK hydration race) → auth store treats as logged out → router guard redirects to /login. Fix: in auth.ts init(), fall back to parsing sFrontToken cookie payload if SDK says no session — if its `up.exp` (session exp ms) is in the future, mark sessionExists=true and read orgId via subsequent /api/v1/me call. SDK catches up shortly after.

gh pr create --title "fix(spa): use sFrontToken cookie as cold-boot session fallback" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
Fixes the long-running **'logout on navigation' bug**: hard browser navigation (page reload, address-bar navigation, OAuth redirect-back) to a protected route bounced the user to `/login` despite valid SuperTokens cookies being present.

## Root cause
On cold boot, `Session.doesSessionExist()` returns `false` before the supertokens-web-js SDK has hydrated its internal state from cookies. Sequence:

1. `auth.init()` calls `Session.doesSessionExist()` → returns `false` (race)
2. `sessionExists.value = false`
3. `app.mount('#app')` resolves initial route
4. Router guard sees `!isAuthenticated`, returns `'/login'`
5. SDK finishes hydrating, subsequent calls return `true` — but redirect already happened

Verified by reading `__supertokensSessionRecipe.doesSessionExist()` after the redirect: returns `true`, Pinia state shows authenticated, cookies all present. Hard truth was that the guard ran during the race window.

## Fix
After the SDK probe, fall back to parsing the `sFrontToken` cookie directly. If its embedded session expiry (`up.exp`) is in the future, trust the cookie and set `sessionExists = true`. The SDK catches up; the next authenticated API call works normally (and refreshes if needed).

The cookie is the same `sFrontToken` the SDK itself writes/reads via its default `cookieHandler`, so this is just reading from the SDK's storage one frame earlier.

## Test plan
- [x] Local typecheck + lint + unit tests pass
- [x] Hot-deployed bundle to demo box, verified end-to-end:
  - Hard-nav to `/raven/dashboard` → stays
  - Hard-nav to `/raven/settings` → stays
  - Hard-nav to `/raven/api-keys` → stays
  - Authed `GET /raven/api/v1/orgs/:id` returns 200
- [ ] CI green
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -5

**Done.** PR #673 queued for auto-merge.

## What was wrong (recap)

The real bug was never SuperTokens at all — three layers fooled us:

1. **`docker.yml` path filter** excluded `frontend/src/**` → PR #670 (header-mode) merged but no image was ever rebuilt with the new code. Fixed in PR #671.
2. **`FRONTEND_IMAGE` on the box** pointed at orphan `frontend:raven-self-contained` instead of the path-prefixed `frontend-raven:main`. Repointed.
3. **Actual culprit**: SPA's `auth.init()` raced with the supertokens-web-js SDK's internal cookie hydration on cold page loads. `Session.doesSessionExist()` returned `false` for a split second, the router guard fired, redirect to `/login` happened before the SDK caught up.

The PR #672 backend pin to `HeaderTransferMethod` is harmless but turned out to be unnecessary for fixing the bug — the SDK was already in header-on-the-wire mode. Real fix: cookie-fallback in `auth.init()` (PR #673).

## What lands on next CI cycle

When #673 merges, the broadened path filter from #671 triggers `docker.yml` → fresh `frontend-raven:main` image (built by CI, replaces my hot-deployed bundle). Box keeps pulling `:main` so it'll pick up automatically next time we deploy/redeploy frontend.

Want me to cut a release tag to fully run the demo-deploy workflow against this, or leave as-is for now?

content.subject: Follow-up: fix cosign signing config conflicts in release.yml
content.description: Two release.yml jobs failing on cosign v2 breaking change: 'Go binaries' (goreleaser-managed cosign step) and 'Frontend bundle' (direct cosign sign-blob step). Both error: 'cannot specify service URLs and use signing config'. Newer cosign rejects --oidc-issuer when a signing-config is present. Fix: either remove --oidc-issuer flag (let signing-config provide it) OR pin cosign to older version. Replace deprecated --output-signature/--output-certificate with --bundle. NOT blocking demo-deploy — these are for GitHub Release artifacts only. Separate PR.

content.subject: Follow-up: populate users.email from Google session claims
content.description: Real user row in users table has empty email after Google OAuth. supertokens.go's extractSessionClaims reads from AccessTokenPayload but the payload doesn't include email by default. Need OverrideAPIs.SignInUpPost or a backend post-signinup hook that writes email/name from the ThirdParty user info into the SuperTokens session payload (so downstream userLookup gets real values). Separate PR — diagnostic + fix.

content.subject: Diagnose mid-session logout on navigation
content.description: Verified via Playwright: header-mode is correctly wired (st-auth-mode: header sent in request headers, frontend bundle has tokenTransferMethod:`header` baked in, redirect URI matches Google Console). What I CANNOT test from Playwright: actual Google sign-in (no real account / 2FA). Needs user to (a) clear all browser data, (b) sign in fresh, (c) confirm header-mode tokens land in localStorage (st-access-token, st-refresh-token), (d) try the navigation again. If still fails post-clear-and-fresh-sign-in, the issue isn't cookie-related and is likely a backend session-validation or anti-csrf mismatch.

content.subject: Trigger docker.yml on main HEAD to rebuild frontend with header-mode bundle
content.description: PR #670 (header-based session transfer) is merged into main (ebf76654) but never built an image — docker.yml path filter excludes frontend/src/**. Manual dispatch needed to publish a fresh :raven-self-contained.

content.subject: Fix docker.yml paths filter to include source dirs (frontend/src, ai-worker python, etc.)
content.description: Current filter only triggers on Dockerfile / nginx.conf / docker-compose changes. Any TS/Vue change to frontend/src or Go change cmd/... or Python change to ai-worker/raven_worker/** silently skips the image build, leaving the floating :main / :raven-self-contained tags stale relative to source. Needs paths broadened (or split workflow: lint/test on every push, image build gated separately).

content.subject: Backend: pin SuperTokens to header transfer in session.Init (GetTokenTransferMethod)
content.description: SPA is in header mode but backend defaults to cookie response on OAuth callback. Pin via session.Init's GetTokenTransferMethod returning HeaderTransferMethod so the OAuth signinup response surfaces tokens in headers (not cookies), which the SDK then writes to localStorage. Required for the SPA's Session.doesSessionExist() to return true after page reload / mid-session navigation.
content.activeForm: Pinning backend SuperTokens to header transfer

content.subject: Frontend: fix auth.init() cold-boot race — use sFrontToken cookie as fallback
content.description: On cold page load with valid SuperTokens cookies, Session.doesSessionExist() returns false initially (SDK hydration race) → auth store treats as logged out → router guard redirects to /login. Fix: in auth.ts init(), fall back to parsing sFrontToken cookie payload if SDK says no session — if its `up.exp` (session exp ms) is in the future, mark sessionExists=true and read orgId via subsequent /api/v1/me call. SDK catches up shortly after.

content.subject: Backend: pin SuperTokens to header transfer in session.Init (GetTokenTransferMethod)

SDK catches up shortly after.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify every commit being pushed carries a Signed-off-by trailer.
# Mirrors the .github DCO check so failures surface locally instead of in CI.
#
# Install once per clone:
#   git config core.hooksPath .githooks

set -euo pipefail

zero='0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'

while IFS=' ' read -r _local_ref local_sha _remote_ref remote_sha; do
    # Branch deletion — nothing to verify.
    if [ "$local_sha" = "$zero" ]; then
        continue
    fi

    if [ "$remote_sha" = "$zero" ]; then
        # New branch on the remote — verify everything since the merge-base
        # with origin/main (or main if origin/main is missing).
        if base=$(git merge-base origin/main "$local_sha" 2>/dev/null); then
            range="${base}..${local_sha}"
        elif base=$(git merge-base main "$local_sha" 2>/dev/null); then
            range="${base}..${local_sha}"
        else
            # No mergeable base; check the last 50 commits as a safety net.
            range="${local_sha}~50..${local_sha}"
        fi
    else
        range="${remote_sha}..${local_sha}"
    fi

    missing=0
    while read -r sha; do
        [ -z "$sha" ] && continue
        if ! git log -1 --format='%B' "$sha" | grep -qE '^Signed-off-by: .+ <.+@.+>'; then
            author=$(git log -1 --format='%an <%ae>' "$sha")
            subject=$(git log -1 --format='%s' "$sha")
            echo "ERROR: ${sha:0:8} by ${author} missing Signed-off-by"
            echo "       ${subject}"
            missing=1
        fi
    done < <(git rev-list "$range" 2>/dev/null || true)

    if [ "$missing" -ne 0 ]; then
        cat >&2 <<'EOF'

Refusing to push: one or more commits lack a Signed-off-by trailer.

Fix the entire branch in one shot with:
    git rebase origin/main --exec 'git commit --amend --no-edit -s'
    git push --force-with-lease

For a single new commit, just use:
    git commit -s -m "..."

EOF
        exit 1
    fi
done

exit 0

set -euo pipefail

zero='0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'

# ── frontend lint gate ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Runs once per push if any commit being sent touches frontend/. CI's
# Frontend CI workflow runs `npm run lint`, so any miss here lands as a
# PR-blocking red check minutes later — annoying enough to be worth a
# few seconds locally. Skipped if npm is unavailable (CI containers,
# fresh checkouts before `npm install`).
frontend_lint_if_needed() {
    if ! command -v npm > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        return 0
    fi
    if [ ! -d frontend ]; then
        return 0
    fi

    # Collect every revision range from the push payload (stdin was already
    # consumed by the DCO loop, so this is invoked separately below with the
    # ranges captured into an array).
    local touched=0
    for range in "$@"; do
        if git diff --name-only "$range" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^frontend/'; then
            touched=1
            break
        fi
    done
    if [ "$touched" -eq 0 ]; then
        return 0
    fi

    echo "pre-push: running 'npm run lint' (frontend/ touched)..."
    if ! (cd frontend && npm run --silent lint > /tmp/raven-pre-push-lint.log 2>&1); then
        cat /tmp/raven-pre-push-lint.log >&2
        cat >&2 <<'EOF'

Refusing to push: frontend ESLint failed. Fix the errors above (or
`cd frontend && npm run lint:fix` for the auto-fixable ones), commit
the result, then re-push.
EOF
        return 1
    fi
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify every commit being pushed carries a Signed-off-by trailer AND,
# when the push touches frontend/, that ESLint passes. Mirrors the
# .github DCO + Frontend CI lint gates so failures surface locally
# instead of in CI.
#
# Install once per clone:
#   git config core.hooksPath .githooks

set -euo pipefail

zero='0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'

# ── frontend lint gate ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Runs once per push if any commit being sent touches frontend/. CI's
# Frontend CI workflow runs `npm run lint`, so any miss here lands as a
# PR-blocking red check minutes later — annoying enough to be worth a
# few seconds locally. Skipped if npm is unavailable (CI containers,
# fresh checkouts before `npm install`).
frontend_lint_if_needed() {
    if ! command -v npm > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        return 0
    fi
    if [ ! -d frontend ]; then
        return 0
    fi

    # Collect every revision range from the push payload (stdin was already
    # consumed by the DCO loop, so this is invoked separately below with the
    # ranges captured into an array).
    local touched=0
    for range in "$@"; do
        if git diff --name-only "$range" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^frontend/'; then
            touched=1
            break
        fi
    done
    if [ "$touched" -eq 0 ]; then
        return 0
    fi

    echo "pre-push: running 'npm run lint' (frontend/ touched)..."
    if ! (cd frontend && npm run --silent lint > /tmp/raven-pre-push-lint.log 2>&1); then
        cat /tmp/raven-pre-push-lint.log >&2
        cat >&2 <<'EOF'

Refusing to push: frontend ESLint failed. Fix the errors above (or
`cd frontend && npm run lint:fix` for the auto-fixable ones), commit
the result, then re-push.
EOF
        return 1
    fi
}

ranges=()

while IFS=' ' read -r _local_ref local_sha _remote_ref remote_sha; do
    # Branch deletion — nothing to verify.
    if [ "$local_sha" = "$zero" ]; then
        continue
    fi

    if [ "$remote_sha" = "$zero" ]; then
        # New branch on the remote — verify everything since the merge-base
        # with origin/main (or main if origin/main is missing).
        if base=$(git merge-base origin/main "$local_sha" 2>/dev/null); then
            range="${base}..${local_sha}"
        elif base=$(git merge-base main "$local_sha" 2>/dev/null); then
            range="${base}..${local_sha}"
        else
            # No mergeable base; check the last 50 commits as a safety net.
            range="${local_sha}~50..${local_sha}"
        fi
    else
        range="${remote_sha}..${local_sha}"
    fi
    ranges+=("$range")

    missing=0
    while read -r sha; do
        [ -z "$sha" ] && continue
        if ! git log -1 --format='%B' "$sha" | grep -qE '^Signed-off-by: .+ <.+@.+>'; then
            author=$(git log -1 --format='%an <%ae>' "$sha")
            subject=$(git log -1 --format='%s' "$sha")
            echo "ERROR: ${sha:0:8} by ${author} missing Signed-off-by"
            echo "       ${subject}"
            missing=1
        fi
    done < <(git rev-list "$range" 2>/dev/null || true)

    if [ "$missing" -ne 0 ]; then
        cat >&2 <<'EOF'

Refusing to push: one or more commits lack a Signed-off-by trailer.

Fix the entire branch in one shot with:
    git rebase origin/main --exec 'git commit --amend --no-edit -s'
    git push --force-with-lease

For a single new commit, just use:
    git commit -s -m "..."

EOF
        exit 1
    fi
done

exit 0

content.description: Two release.yml jobs failing on cosign v2 breaking change: 'Go binaries' (goreleaser-managed cosign step) and 'Frontend bundle' (direct cosign sign-blob step). Both error: 'cannot specify service URLs and use signing config'. Newer cosign rejects --oidc-issuer when a signing-config is present. Fix: either remove --oidc-issuer flag (let signing-config provide it) OR pin cosign to older version. Replace deprecated --output-signature/--output-certificate with --bundle. NOT blocking demo-deploy — these are for GitHub Release artifacts only. Separate PR.

content.subject: Follow-up: populate users.email from Google session claims
content.description: Real user row in users table has empty email after Google OAuth. supertokens.go's extractSessionClaims reads from AccessTokenPayload but the payload doesn't include email by default. Need OverrideAPIs.SignInUpPost or a backend post-signinup hook that writes email/name from the ThirdParty user info into the SuperTokens session payload (so downstream userLookup gets real values). Separate PR — diagnostic + fix.

content.subject: Diagnose mid-session logout on navigation
content.description: Verified via Playwright: header-mode is correctly wired (st-auth-mode: header sent in request headers, frontend bundle has tokenTransferMethod:`header` baked in, redirect URI matches Google Console). What I CANNOT test from Playwright: actual Google sign-in (no real account / 2FA). Needs user to (a) clear all browser data, (b) sign in fresh, (c) confirm header-mode tokens land in localStorage (st-access-token, st-refresh-token), (d) try the navigation again. If still fails post-clear-and-fresh-sign-in, the issue isn't cookie-related and is likely a backend session-validation or anti-csrf mismatch.

content.subject: Trigger docker.yml on main HEAD to rebuild frontend with header-mode bundle
content.description: PR #670 (header-based session transfer) is merged into main (ebf76654) but never built an image — docker.yml path filter excludes frontend/src/**. Manual dispatch needed to publish a fresh :raven-self-contained.

content.subject: Fix docker.yml paths filter to include source dirs (frontend/src, ai-worker python, etc.)
content.description: Current filter only triggers on Dockerfile / nginx.conf / docker-compose changes. Any TS/Vue change to frontend/src or Go change cmd/... or Python change to ai-worker/raven_worker/** silently skips the image build, leaving the floating :main / :raven-self-contained tags stale relative to source. Needs paths broadened (or split workflow: lint/test on every push, image build gated separately).

content.subject: Backend: pin SuperTokens to header transfer in session.Init (GetTokenTransferMethod)
content.description: SPA is in header mode but backend defaults to cookie response on OAuth callback. Pin via session.Init's GetTokenTransferMethod returning HeaderTransferMethod so the OAuth signinup response surfaces tokens in headers (not cookies), which the SDK then writes to localStorage. Required for the SPA's Session.doesSessionExist() to return true after page reload / mid-session navigation.
content.activeForm: Pinning backend SuperTokens to header transfer

content.subject: Frontend: fix auth.init() cold-boot race — use sFrontToken cookie as fallback
content.description: On cold page load with valid SuperTokens cookies, Session.doesSessionExist() returns false initially (SDK hydration race) → auth store treats as logged out → router guard redirects to /login. Fix: in auth.ts init(), fall back to parsing sFrontToken cookie payload if SDK says no session — if its `up.exp` (session exp ms) is in the future, mark sessionExists=true and read orgId via subsequent /api/v1/me call. SDK catches up shortly after.

content.subject: URGENT: fix PR #625 — mount ALL routes under root group
content.description: PR #625 only moved /healthz under `root := router.Group(cfg.Server.PathPrefix)`. All other registrations still on bare `router`. Result: every /raven/api/v1/* request 404s in prod RIGHT NOW. Fix: replace `router.GET/POST/Group/...` with `root.GET/POST/Group/...` for every route registration (keep middleware `.Use()` on router). For PathPrefix="" the behavior is unchanged. Add a smoke test that hits a public route with PathPrefix set so this never regresses.

content.description: Single PR fixing: (1) release.yml manifest printf for multi-arch, (2) demo-deploy.yml strip v-prefix from tag, (3) demo-deploy.yml smoke URL to demo.ravencloak.org/raven/api/v1/config, (4) release.yml frontend matrix entry building VITE_BASE_PATH=/raven/ variant tagged frontend:VERSION-raven. content.subject: Follow-up: fix cosign signing config conflicts in release.yml
content.description: Two release.yml jobs failing on cosign v2 breaking change: 'Go binaries' (goreleaser-managed cosign step) and 'Frontend bundle' (direct cosign sign-blob step). Both error: 'cannot specify service URLs and use signing config'. Newer cosign rejects --oidc-issuer when a signing-config is present. Fix: either remove --oidc-issuer flag (let signing-config provide it) OR pin cosign to older version. Replace deprecated --output-signature/--output-certificate with --bundle. NOT blocking demo-deploy — these are for GitHub Release artifacts only. Separate PR.

content.subject: Follow-up: populate users.email from Google session claims
content.description: Real user row in users table has empty email after Google OAuth. supertokens.go's extractSessionClaims reads from AccessTokenPayload but the payload doesn't include email by default. Need OverrideAPIs.SignInUpPost or a backend post-signinup hook that writes email/name from the ThirdParty user info into the SuperTokens session payload (so downstream userLookup gets real values). Separate PR — diagnostic + fix.

content.subject: Diagnose mid-session logout on navigation
content.description: Verified via Playwright: header-mode is correctly wired (st-auth-mode: header sent in request headers, frontend bundle has tokenTransferMethod:`header` baked in, redirect URI matches Google Console). What I CANNOT test from Playwright: actual Google sign-in (no real account / 2FA). Needs user to (a) clear all browser data, (b) sign in fresh, (c) confirm header-mode tokens land in localStorage (st-access-token, st-refresh-token), (d) try the navigation again. If still fails post-clear-and-fresh-sign-in, the issue isn't cookie-related and is likely a backend session-validation or anti-csrf mismatch.

content.subject: Trigger docker.yml on main HEAD to rebuild frontend with header-mode bundle
content.description: PR #670 (header-based session transfer) is merged into main (ebf76654) but never built an image — docker.yml path filter excludes frontend/src/**. Manual dispatch needed to publish a fresh :raven-self-contained.

content.subject: Fix docker.yml paths filter to include source dirs (frontend/src, ai-worker python, etc.)
content.description: Current filter only triggers on Dockerfile / nginx.conf / docker-compose changes. Any TS/Vue change to frontend/src or Go change cmd/... or Python change to ai-worker/raven_worker/** silently skips the image build, leaving the floating :main / :raven-self-contained tags stale relative to source. Needs paths broadened (or split workflow: lint/test on every push, image build gated separately).

content.subject: Backend: pin SuperTokens to header transfer in session.Init (GetTokenTransferMethod)
content.description: SPA is in header mode but backend defaults to cookie response on OAuth callback. Pin via session.Init's GetTokenTransferMethod returning HeaderTransferMethod so the OAuth signinup response surfaces tokens in headers (not cookies), which the SDK then writes to localStorage. Required for the SPA's Session.doesSessionExist() to return true after page reload / mid-session navigation.
content.activeForm: Pinning backend SuperTokens to header transfer

content.subject: Frontend: fix auth.init() cold-boot race — use sFrontToken cookie as fallback
content.description: On cold page load with valid SuperTokens cookies, Session.doesSessionExist() returns false initially (SDK hydration race) → auth store treats as logged out → router guard redirects to /login. Fix: in auth.ts init(), fall back to parsing sFrontToken cookie payload if SDK says no session — if its `up.exp` (session exp ms) is in the future, mark sessionExists=true and read orgId via subsequent /api/v1/me call. SDK catches up shortly after.

# Builds the Go binaries (cmd/api, cmd/worker), produces SHA256SUMS and
# tar/zip archives, and signs the checksums manifest with cosign keyless.

# Invoked by .github/workflows/release.yml on tag push (v*.*.*).

project_name: raven

before:
  hooks:
    - go mod tidy
--
# checksums.txt.pem recorded in the Rekor transparency log.
signs:
  - id: cosign-checksums
    cmd: cosign
    signature: "${artifact}.sig"
    certificate: "${artifact}.pem"
    args:
      - "sign-blob"
      - "--oidc-issuer=https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
      - "--output-certificate=${certificate}"
      - "--output-signature=${signature}"
      - "${artifact}"
      - "--yes"
    artifacts: checksum

content.subject: Diagnose mid-session logout on navigation
content.description: Verified via Playwright: header-mode is correctly wired (st-auth-mode: header sent in request headers, frontend bundle has tokenTransferMethod:`header` baked in, redirect URI matches Google Console). What I CANNOT test from Playwright: actual Google sign-in (no real account / 2FA). Needs user to (a) clear all browser data, (b) sign in fresh, (c) confirm header-mode tokens land in localStorage (st-access-token, st-refresh-token), (d) try the navigation again. If still fails post-clear-and-fresh-sign-in, the issue isn't cookie-related and is likely a backend session-validation or anti-csrf mismatch.

Needs paths broadened (or split workflow: lint/test on every push, image build gated separately).

content.subject: Backend: pin SuperTokens to header transfer in session.Init (GetTokenTransferMethod)
content.description: SPA is in header mode but backend defaults to cookie response on OAuth callback. Pin via session.Init's GetTokenTransferMethod returning HeaderTransferMethod so the OAuth signinup response surfaces tokens in headers (not cookies), which the SDK then writes to localStorage. Required for the SPA's Session.doesSessionExist() to return true after page reload / mid-session navigation.

content.subject: Frontend: fix auth.init() cold-boot race — use sFrontToken cookie as fallback
content.description: On cold page load with valid SuperTokens cookies, Session.doesSessionExist() returns false initially (SDK hydration race) → auth store treats as logged out → router guard redirects to /login. Fix: in auth.ts init(), fall back to parsing sFrontToken cookie payload if SDK says no session — if its `up.exp` (session exp ms) is in the future, mark sessionExists=true and read orgId via subsequent /api/v1/me call. SDK catches up shortly after.

# GoReleaser configuration for Raven.
# Builds the Go binaries (cmd/api, cmd/worker), produces SHA256SUMS and
# tar/zip archives, and signs the checksums manifest with cosign keyless.
#
# Invoked by .github/workflows/release.yml on tag push (v*.*.*).
# GitHub Release creation is delegated to the workflow so Docker images
# and the frontend bundle can be attached to the same release.

version: 2

project_name: raven

before:
  hooks:
    - go mod tidy

builds:
  - id: raven-api
    main: ./cmd/api
    binary: raven-api
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    goos:
      - linux
      - darwin
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    ignore:
      # Keep the matrix lean — darwin/amd64 dropped since production targets
      # are linux (cloud + Raspberry Pi) plus Apple Silicon for dev.
      - goos: darwin
        goarch: amd64
    flags:
      - -trimpath
    ldflags:
      - -s -w
      - -X main.version={{.Version}}
      - -X main.commit={{.Commit}}
      - -X main.date={{.Date}}

  - id: raven-worker
    main: ./cmd/worker
    binary: raven-worker
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    goos:
      - linux
      - darwin
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    ignore:
      - goos: darwin
        goarch: amd64
    flags:
      - -trimpath
    ldflags:
      - -s -w
      - -X main.version={{.Version}}
      - -X main.commit={{.Commit}}
      - -X main.date={{.Date}}

archives:
  - id: default
    ids:
      - raven-api
      - raven-worker
    name_template: >-
      {{ .ProjectName }}_
      {{- .Version }}_
      {{- .Os }}_
      {{- .Arch }}
    formats: [tar.gz]
    format_overrides:
      - goos: windows
        formats: [zip]
    files:
      - LICENSE
      - README.md
      - SECURITY.md

checksum:
  name_template: "checksums.txt"
  algorithm: sha256

# cosign keyless signing (OIDC). Produces checksums.txt.sig and
# checksums.txt.pem recorded in the Rekor transparency log.
signs:
  - id: cosign-checksums
    cmd: cosign
    signature: "${artifact}.sig"
    certificate: "${artifact}.pem"
    args:
      - "sign-blob"
      - "--oidc-issuer=https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
      - "--output-certificate=${certificate}"
      - "--output-signature=${signature}"
      - "${artifact}"
      - "--yes"
    artifacts: checksum
    output: true

snapshot:
  version_template: "{{ incpatch .Version }}-next"

# Let release.yml publish the GitHub Release — goreleaser only builds
# artifacts and writes them to dist/.
release:
  disable: true

## Why
cosign v3.0+ derives the OIDC issuer (plus Fulcio/Rekor URLs) from the bundled Sigstore signing config. Passing `--oidc-issuer` alongside it trips:

```
Error: cannot specify service URLs and use signing config
```

That blocked both **v0.3.0-rc1** and the **post-merge tag run** for *Go binaries* (.goreleaser.yaml sign-blob) and *Frontend bundle* (release.yml sign-blob).

## Changes
- `.goreleaser.yaml`: remove `--oidc-issuer=https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com` from the `signs[0].args` for the checksum file.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: same removal from the frontend bundle's `cosign sign-blob` step.

Both default to the same GHA OIDC issuer when omitted, so the keyless flow is functionally unchanged.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] After landing, cut a fresh tag and confirm Go binaries + Frontend bundle complete (both should produce `.sig` + `.pem` artifacts)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

Needs user to (a) clear all browser data, (b) sign in fresh, (c) confirm header-mode tokens land in localStorage (st-access-token, st-refresh-token), (d) try the navigation again. If still fails post-clear-and-fresh-sign-in, the issue isn't cookie-related and is likely a backend session-validation or anti-csrf mismatch.

content.subject: Backend: pin SuperTokens to header transfer in session.Init (GetTokenTransferMethod)

Pin via session.Init's GetTokenTransferMethod returning HeaderTransferMethod so the OAuth signinup response surfaces tokens in headers (not cookies), which the SDK then writes to localStorage. Required for the SPA's Session.doesSessionExist() to return true after page reload / mid-session navigation.

content.subject: Frontend: fix auth.init() cold-boot race — use sFrontToken cookie as fallback

Fix: in auth.ts init(), fall back to parsing sFrontToken cookie payload if SDK says no session — if its `up.exp` (session exp ms) is in the future, mark sessionExists=true and read orgId via subsequent /api/v1/me call. SDK catches up shortly after.

1	package handler
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"net/http"
7	
8		"github.com/gin-gonic/gin"
9		"github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/internal/middleware"
10		"github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/internal/model"
11		"github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/pkg/apierror"
12	)
13	
14	// AuthServicer is the interface the auth handler requires from the user service.
15	type AuthServicer interface {
16		GetByExternalID(ctx context.Context, externalID string) (*model.User, error)
17		Create(ctx context.Context, externalID, email, displayName string) (*model.User, error)
18	}
19	
20	// DemoOrgJoiner is an optional interface that auto-joins new users to the demo
21	// organisation as viewers. When nil, the auto-join step is skipped.
22	type DemoOrgJoiner interface {
23		// JoinDemoOrg adds the user as a viewer to the first workspace of the demo org.
24		// Returns silently on any error (best-effort).
25		JoinDemoOrg(ctx context.Context, userID string)
26	}
27	
28	// AuthHandler handles authentication callback endpoints.
29	type AuthHandler struct {
30		svc      AuthServicer
31		demoJoin DemoOrgJoiner
32	}
33	
34	// NewAuthHandler creates a new AuthHandler.
35	// Pass optional DemoOrgJoiner instances (at most one) to enable auto-join on signup.
36	func NewAuthHandler(svc AuthServicer, opts ...DemoOrgJoiner) *AuthHandler {
37		h := &AuthHandler{svc: svc}
38		if len(opts) > 0 {
39			h.demoJoin = opts[0]
40		}
41		return h
42	}
43	
44	// Callback handles POST /api/v1/auth/callback.
45	// Called by the frontend after OIDC redirect callback completes.
46	// Returns whether the user is new (needs onboarding) or existing.
47	func (h *AuthHandler) Callback(c *gin.Context) {
48		externalID, _ := c.Get(string(middleware.ContextKeyExternalID))
49		externalIDStr, _ := externalID.(string)
50		if externalIDStr == "" {
51			_ = c.Error(apierror.NewUnauthorized("missing external identity"))
52			c.Abort()
53			return
54		}
55	
56		email, _ := c.Get(string(middleware.ContextKeyEmail))
57		emailStr, _ := email.(string)
58		name, _ := c.Get(string(middleware.ContextKeyUserName))
59		nameStr, _ := name.(string)
60	
61		// Check if user exists
62		user, err := h.svc.GetByExternalID(c.Request.Context(), externalIDStr)
63		if err != nil {
64			// Check if it's a not-found error (service wraps as apierror)
65			var appErr *apierror.AppError
66			isNotFound := errors.As(err, &appErr) && appErr.Code == http.StatusNotFound
67			if !isNotFound {
68				_ = c.Error(apierror.NewInternal("failed to look up user: " + err.Error()))
69				c.Abort()
70				return
71			}
72			// User not found — first login, create record with nil org_id
73			user, err = h.svc.Create(c.Request.Context(), externalIDStr, emailStr, nameStr)
74			if err != nil {
75				_ = c.Error(apierror.NewInternal("failed to create user: " + err.Error()))
76				c.Abort()
77				return
78			}
79	
80			// Auto-join demo org as viewer (best-effort, non-blocking).
81			if h.demoJoin != nil {
82				h.demoJoin.JoinDemoOrg(c.Request.Context(), user.ID)
83			}
84	
85			c.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{"isNewUser": true, "userId": user.ID})
86			return
87		}
88	
89		// Existing user
90		if user.OrgID == nil {
91			// Abandoned onboarding — also try auto-join in case they missed it.
92			if h.demoJoin != nil {
93				h.demoJoin.JoinDemoOrg(c.Request.Context(), user.ID)
94			}
95			c.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{"isNewUser": true, "userId": user.ID})
96			return
97		}
98	
99		c.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{
100			"isNewUser": false,
101			"orgId":     *user.OrgID,
102			"userId":    user.ID,
103		})
104	}

content.subject: Backend: pin SuperTokens to header transfer in session.Init (GetTokenTransferMethod)

Pin via session.Init's GetTokenTransferMethod returning HeaderTransferMethod so the OAuth signinup response surfaces tokens in headers (not cookies), which the SDK then writes to localStorage. Required for the SPA's Session.doesSessionExist() to return true after page reload / mid-session navigation.

content.subject: Frontend: fix auth.init() cold-boot race — use sFrontToken cookie as fallback
content.description: On cold page load with valid SuperTokens cookies, Session.doesSessionExist() returns false initially (SDK hydration race) → auth store treats as logged out → router guard redirects to /login. Fix: in auth.ts init(), fall back to parsing sFrontToken cookie payload if SDK says no session — if its `up.exp` (session exp ms) is in the future, mark sessionExists=true and read orgId via subsequent /api/v1/me call. SDK catches up shortly after.

content.subject: Frontend: fix auth.init() cold-boot race — use sFrontToken cookie as fallback
content.description: On cold page load with valid SuperTokens cookies, Session.doesSessionExist() returns false initially (SDK hydration race) → auth store treats as logged out → router guard redirects to /login. Fix: in auth.ts init(), fall back to parsing sFrontToken cookie payload if SDK says no session — if its `up.exp` (session exp ms) is in the future, mark sessionExists=true and read orgId via subsequent /api/v1/me call. SDK catches up shortly after.

input.command:
gh pr create --title "fix(auth): populate users.email on first Google login via SuperTokens core lookup" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem
Every Google signup landed in our `users` table with `email = ''`. The Callback handler reads email from the session payload (via `SessionMiddleware`), but SuperTokens' ThirdParty (Google) recipe doesn't embed provider claims into the access-token JWT — only `sub`, `iss`, `exp`, session bookkeeping. So our `extractSessionClaims` always returned an empty email for Google logins.

Downstream effects:
- Welcome mails (planned) have nowhere to send to
- Audit log identity is anonymous-looking
- The eventual `GET /api/v1/me` response is missing the canonical address

## Fix
When the session claims don't carry an email, look up the SuperTokens core's user record via `thirdparty.GetUserByID` and use the email from there.

### Wiring
- New optional `EmailLookup` interface on `AuthHandler` (mirrors the `DemoOrgJoiner` pattern — handler stays usable in tests where SuperTokens isn't running)
- `NewAuthHandler`'s opts becomes `...any` with a type-switch so callers can pass `DemoOrgJoiner` / `EmailLookup` in any order
- `SuperTokensProvider` implements the interface using the existing `thirdparty` recipe

## Cost
One extra SuperTokens-core call per **signin** (not per request). Negligible.

## Existing users
Not backfilled by this PR — affected rows get fixed organically the next time the user signs in. If a faster backfill is needed, a one-off SQL migration that pulls emails from the SuperTokens core's `thirdparty_users` table will do it.

## Test plan
- [x] Unit tests for: fallback fires when claims empty, lookup is skipped when claims have email, nil/failing lookup degrades gracefully (3 cases, ~0.8s)
- [x] `go vet` + `golangci-lint --new-from-rev=HEAD` clean
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Sign in via Google on demo, check `users.email` is populated
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

git commit -s -m "fix(api): set Cache-Control: no-store on every /api/v1 response

Authenticated GET responses had no Cache-Control header, so browsers
and shared HTTP caches pinned them by default. Caught via end-to-end
Playwright trace against the demo box: GET .../documents with no query
string returned total=1 while the DB had two rows — same cf-ray on
repeated hits meant the browser disk cache was serving a stale response
from before the second document was uploaded. Adding ?nocache=… bypassed
the cache and returned the correct total=2.

This is a broader bug than the document list: every list/get endpoint
under /api/v1 was at risk of serving stale state after writes through
the same SPA session, and (worse) sensitive responses could leak from
a shared browser cache.

Adds a tiny NoStoreAPI middleware that sets the conventional JSON-API
trio:

    Cache-Control: no-store, max-age=0, private, must-revalidate
    Pragma: no-cache
    Expires: 0

Mounted on the api.Group(\"/api/v1\") before everything else so the
headers ship on every code path (including 401s and error returns).

Unit test pins the exact header set to prevent silent weakening." 2>&1 | tail -3

git push -u origin fix/api-no-store-cache-headers 2>&1 | tail -3 && gh pr create --title "fix(api): set Cache-Control: no-store on every /api/v1 response" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem
Authenticated GET responses carried no `Cache-Control` header, so browsers (and shared HTTP caches) pinned them by default. Caught via end-to-end Playwright trace against the demo box:

```
GET .../documents                    → total: 1  (DB actually has 2 rows; browser cache hit, same cf-ray on retries)
GET .../documents?nocache=<ts>       → total: 2  (cache miss → origin)
```

This is **broader than document listing** — every list/get endpoint under `/api/v1` was vulnerable to:
1. Stale UI state after the SPA wrote / uploaded / deleted in the same session
2. Sensitive responses sticking in shared browser caches (multi-user laptop, etc.)

## Fix
Tiny `NoStoreAPI` middleware mounted on `api.Group("/api/v1")` before everything else, so the headers ship on every code path (including 401s, error returns, single-user mode):

```
Cache-Control: no-store, max-age=0, private, must-revalidate
Pragma: no-cache
Expires: 0
```

Unit test pins the exact header set to prevent silent weakening (e.g. someone setting just `no-cache` which still allows storage with revalidation).

## Test plan
- [x] `go test ./internal/middleware/... -run TestNoStoreAPI` passes
- [x] `go vet` + `golangci-lint --new-from-rev=HEAD` clean
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Post-merge on demo: confirm `Cache-Control: no-store` shows up on `GET /raven/api/v1/...`, and the documents list reports the correct total without `?nocache=` hacks
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

# Raven — EC2 server deployment
#
# Runs on a secondary Docker daemon (hidden from default docker ps).
# Cloudflare Tunnel handles all inbound traffic — no ports exposed to the internet.
#
# Usage:
#   DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/raven/docker.sock \
#   docker compose -f deploy/ec2/docker-compose.server.yml --env-file .env.server up -d

services:
  # ─── Frontend (Vue SPA served via nginx) ───────────────────────────────────
  frontend:
    image: ${FRONTEND_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/frontend:latest}
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:3080:8080"
    networks:
      - raven-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:8080/healthz"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3

  # ─── Go API ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  go-api:
    image: ${GO_API_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/go-api:latest}
    # Bind to loopback only — cloudflared reaches it, internet cannot.
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8081:8081"
    env_file: .env.server
    environment:
      SUPERTOKENS_CONNECTION_URI: "http://supertokens:3567"
      SUPERTOKENS_API_KEY: "${SUPERTOKENS_API_KEY}"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      valkey:
        condition: service_healthy
      supertokens:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:8081/healthz"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 15s
    networks:
      - raven-net
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ─── Python AI Worker (gRPC) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  python-worker:
    image: ${PYTHON_WORKER_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/ravencloak-org/python-worker:latest}
    env_file: .env.server
    environment:
      RAVEN_MEMORY_DIR: /var/raven/memories
    volumes:
      - raven-memories:/var/raven/memories
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      valkey:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      - raven-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    # No external ports — go-api reaches it via Docker network on :50051

  # ─── PostgreSQL + pgvector ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  postgres:
    image: pgvector/pgvector:pg18
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-raven}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-raven}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?POSTGRES_PASSWORD is required}
    volumes:
      - pg-data:/var/lib/postgresql
      - ../../deploy/postgres/init.sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init.sql:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER:-raven} -d ${POSTGRES_DB:-raven}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    networks:
      - raven-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    # No external port — only reachable inside raven-net

  # ─── Valkey ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  valkey:
    image: valkey/valkey:8.1-alpine
    command: ["valkey-server", "--maxmemory", "512mb", "--maxmemory-policy", "allkeys-lru", "--save", "60", "1"]
    volumes:
      - valkey-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "valkey-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5
    networks:
      - raven-net
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ─── SuperTokens Auth Backend ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  supertokens:
    image: registry.supertokens.io/supertokens/supertokens-postgresql
    environment:
      POSTGRESQL_CONNECTION_URI: "postgresql://${POSTGRES_USER:-raven}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-raven}"
      API_KEYS: "${SUPERTOKENS_API_KEY}"
      DISABLE_TELEMETRY: "true"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      - raven-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "sh", "-c", "curl -sf http://localhost:3567/hello || exit 1"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 10s

  # ─── SeaweedFS (object storage) ───────────────────────────────────────────
  seaweedfs-master:
    image: chrislusf/seaweedfs
    command: "master -ip=seaweedfs-master -ip.bind=0.0.0.0"
    networks:
      - raven-net
    restart: unless-stopped

  seaweedfs-volume:
    image: chrislusf/seaweedfs
    command: "volume -mserver=seaweedfs-master:9333 -ip.bind=0.0.0.0 -dir=/data"
    volumes:
      - seaweedfs-data:/data
    depends_on:
      - seaweedfs-master
    networks:
      - raven-net
    restart: unless-stopped

  seaweedfs-filer:
    image: chrislusf/seaweedfs
    command: "filer -master=seaweedfs-master:9333 -ip.bind=0.0.0.0 -s3"
    depends_on:
      - seaweedfs-master
      - seaweedfs-volume
    networks:
      - raven-net
    restart: unless-stopped
    # No external port — go-api reaches it via Docker network

  # ─── OpenObserve (observability) — loopback only ──────────────────────────
  openobserve:
    image: public.ecr.aws/zinclabs/openobserve:latest
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5080:5080"

140	// refineContentType adjusts the detected MIME type based on file extension
141	// for text-based formats that http.DetectContentType cannot distinguish.
142	func refineContentType(detected, filename string) string {
143		// If DetectContentType already identified a non-text type, trust it.
144		if detected != "text/plain; charset=utf-8" &&
145			detected != "application/octet-stream" &&
146			detected != "text/plain" {
147			return detected
148		}
149	
150		// Check file extension for known text-based types.
151		lower := lowerFilename(filename)
152		switch {
153		case hasSuffix(lower, ".md"), hasSuffix(lower, ".markdown"):
154			return "text/markdown"
155		case hasSuffix(lower, ".html"), hasSuffix(lower, ".htm"):
156			return "text/html"
157		case hasSuffix(lower, ".csv"):
158			return "text/csv"
159		case hasSuffix(lower, ".txt"):
160			return "text/plain"
161		case hasSuffix(lower, ".pdf"):
162			return "application/pdf"
163		case hasSuffix(lower, ".docx"):
164			return "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document"
165		case hasSuffix(lower, ".pptx"):
166			return "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation"
167		}
168		return detected
169	}
170	
171	func lowerFilename(name string) string {
172		result := make([]byte, len(name))
173		for i := range len(name) {
174			c := name[i]
175			if c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z' {
176				c += 'a' - 'A'
177			}
178			result[i] = c
179		}
180		return string(result)
181	}
182	
183	func hasSuffix(s, suffix string) bool {
184		return len(s) >= len(suffix) && s[len(s)-len(suffix):] == suffix
185	}

62	// Upload validates, deduplicates, stores, and records a new document upload.
63	func (s *UploadService) Upload(ctx context.Context, params UploadParams) (*model.Document, error) {
64		// Validate file type.
65		if !s.allowedTypes[strings.ToLower(params.FileType)] {
66			return nil, apierror.NewBadRequest(fmt.Sprintf("file type not allowed: %s", params.FileType))
67		}
68	
69		// Validate file size.
70		if params.FileSizeBytes > s.maxSizeBytes {
71			return nil, apierror.NewBadRequest(fmt.Sprintf(
72				"file too large: %d bytes exceeds maximum %d bytes",
73				params.FileSizeBytes, s.maxSizeBytes,
74			))
75		}

75		}
76	
77		// Read entire file to compute hash; buffer in memory.
78		// For very large files we would stream to disk, but at 50 MB max this is fine.
79		data, err := io.ReadAll(params.Reader)
80		if err != nil {
81			return nil, apierror.NewInternal("failed to read uploaded file: " + err.Error())
82		}
83	
84		// Compute SHA-256 hash.
85		hash := sha256.Sum256(data)
86		fileHash := hex.EncodeToString(hash[:])
87	
88		// Check for duplicates within the same KB.
89		var existingDoc *model.Document
90		err = db.WithOrgID(ctx, s.pool, params.OrgID, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
91			var findErr error
92			existingDoc, findErr = s.repo.FindByHash(ctx, tx, params.OrgID, params.KnowledgeBaseID, fileHash)
93			return findErr
94		})
95		if err != nil && !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "no rows") {
96			return nil, apierror.NewInternal("failed to check for duplicate: " + err.Error())
97		}

103			}
104		}
105

107		fid, err := s.store.Upload(ctx, params.FileName, strings.NewReader(string(data)))
108		if err != nil {
109			return nil, apierror.NewInternal("failed to upload to storage: " + err.Error())
110		}
111	
112		// Create document record in DB.
113		fileSizeBytes := params.FileSizeBytes
114		newDoc := &model.Document{
115			OrgID:            params.OrgID,
116			KnowledgeBaseID:  params.KnowledgeBaseID,
117			FileName:         params.FileName,
118			FileType:         params.FileType,
119			FileSizeBytes:    &fileSizeBytes,
120			FileHash:         fileHash,
121			StoragePath:      fid,
122			ProcessingStatus: model.ProcessingStatusQueued,
123			UploadedBy:       params.UploadedBy,
124		}
125		var doc *model.Document
126		err = db.WithOrgID(ctx, s.pool, params.OrgID, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
127			var createErr error
128			doc, createErr = s.repo.Create(ctx, tx, newDoc)
129			return createErr
130		})
131		if err != nil {
132			// Attempt to clean up the stored file on DB failure.
133			_ = s.store.Delete(ctx, fid)
134			return nil, apierror.NewInternal("failed to create document record: " + err.Error())
135		}
136	
137		return doc, nil
138	}

gh pr create --title "feat(deploy): ship the Asynq worker so document processing actually runs" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## TL;DR
The Go side of Raven's background queue was **inert in production from day one**. Documents have been silently piling up in Valkey forever.

## What was broken

### 1. The worker was never deployed
`cmd/worker/main.go` is the Asynq consumer that handles `document:process`, `webhook:delivery`, `airbyte:sync`, `email:summary`, `email:send`. It compiles, has tests, and exists in source — but:

- `Dockerfile` only built `/app/api` (the worker binary was never produced)
- No `worker` service in any `docker-compose.yml`

Every job ever enqueued has just sat in Valkey.

### 2. Upload doesn't enqueue
`UploadService.Upload` inserts the doc row with `processing_status=queued` and returns. The only caller of `EnqueueDocumentProcess` in the entire codebase was `internal/service/seed.go`. So even if a worker had been running, real uploads through the API never made it to the queue.

## Fix
- **Dockerfile**: build `/worker` alongside `/api` in the same multi-stage build; copy both into runtime. `CMD` stays at `/app/api` so the existing `go-api` service is unchanged.
- **`deploy/ec2/docker-compose.server.yml`** + **`docker-compose.yml`**: add `worker` service that reuses `GO_API_IMAGE`, overrides entrypoint to `/app/worker`, depends on postgres + valkey + python-worker.
- **`internal/service/upload.go`**: take a `DocumentProcessEnqueuer` (narrow interface), call `EnqueueDocumentProcess` after the DB insert succeeds. Log + continue on enqueue failure rather than rolling back the row (the file is already in storage; failing the HTTP call would be more confusing than a delayed run).
- **`cmd/api/main.go`**: wire `queueClient` into `NewUploadService`.
- **Tests**: pass `nil` queue (only exercise validation paths).

## Verified live
Hot-compiled `/app/worker` and the new `/app/api`, deployed both to the demo box, manually re-enqueued the two documents that had been stuck for days:

```
queued -> ready (chunks=1) in <1s once worker picked them up
```

## Follow-ups tracked separately
- **#30** URL source crawling (`TypeURLScrape`) — no handler, no enqueuer; fully unimplemented.
- Email summaries require `ALLOW_STUB_EMAIL_SENDER=true` when SES isn't configured, otherwise the worker crashloops on boot. Already set on the demo box; needs to be documented in `deploy/vultr/.env.server.example`.

## Test plan
- [x] Verified hot-deploy on demo: queued docs process to `ready`
- [x] `go test ./internal/service/... -run TestUpload` clean
- [x] `golangci-lint --new-from-rev=HEAD` clean
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Post-merge on demo: container `worker` Up, fresh upload through SPA flows to `ready`
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

**Headline finding**: Document processing has never worked in production. Two separate bugs stacked:

1. **The Asynq worker (`cmd/worker`) was never deployed** — Dockerfile didn't build it, no compose service. Every job ever enqueued sat in Valkey indefinitely.
2. **Uploads didn't actually enqueue** — `UploadService.Upload` wrote the row as `queued` and returned without ever calling `EnqueueDocumentProcess`. Only the demo-seed code path ever enqueued anything.

**Verified the fix end-to-end on the live demo:**
- Cross-compiled and hot-deployed `/app/worker` + new `/app/api`
- Manually re-enqueued the two stuck docs → both went `queued → ready` (`chunks=1`) in <1s
- `ALLOW_STUB_EMAIL_SENDER=true` persisted on the box's `.env.server` so the worker doesn't crashloop on the email-summary registration

**PR #681** queued for auto-merge. Once CI builds the new image and the box pulls, the demo will be processing documents on its own.

**Remaining gap tracked as task #30**: URL source crawling (`TypeURLScrape`) is fully unimplemented — there's a task type defined, but no enqueuer in `SourceService` and no handler in the worker. Pure no-op. Decide whether to implement or remove the UI affordance.

Want me to keep going (URL crawling, or cycle back through the open PRs to make sure they're all merging)?
